looks.name: Vault Wall
looks.oneLine: A twelve-cell lattice of real gold — bars, chains, cuffs, rings — laid flat on a dimmed vitrine, with CASH FOR / GOLD in stencil and one gold plate as the only lit thing on the card.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: dg='tile'. The 4x3 lattice draws on `light`, and because nn10 c1=#2c1c37 (lum 0.016) and c2=#1e0925 are both deep, `light` resolves to the hard-coded #eceef2 — so the wall is a pale grey vitrine, 28px gaps, cells 242x322, each cutout fitted at 0.96 with a real drop shadow (rgba(0,0,0,0.28), blur 26, offset 10/16). Then scrimColor = c1 (lum<0.3) at 0.6. Net effect: twelve gold objects lit on a card, dropped 60% into aubergine — the shutter-down look. Every stat tile and plate over the wall goes solid at rgba(c1,0.9) with #ffffff copy (the engine's panel pass), which is what keeps the small type off the lattice. The ONE light is the accent: exactly one plate — the money band carrying PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE — takes nn10 accent #f5ba08; every other plate stays c1 at 0.9. On jw02 the same build runs with #3e3577 as the scrim and #fec674 as the band. Neither palette is pale, so the 0.72 pale-scrim branch and the ink-body cast branch never fire here; if a pale palette is ever substituted the theme is invalid.
looks.imagery: The wall is the gold deck's own pool (CATEGORY_COPY.gold cuts:['gold-']) filtered by okCut, twelve cells from: gold-bars-stack, gold-bars-row, gold-bars-fan, gold-bar-single, gold-chains-pile, gold-chains, gold-bracelet-cuban, gold-bracelet-pair, gold-necklace-single, gold-rings-scatter, gold-class-ring, gold-earrings-pile, gold-jewelry-mixed, gold-coins-pile, gold-scrap-mixed. No hero cutout sits on top — the wall IS the imagery, and a hero over a wall is the overlapping-pile fault. Marks: line art only, from the gold set (gem, coin, ingot, chain, ringMark), two at most, in the corners, never in the middle, never an emoji.
looks.copy: The pawnbroker with the shutter down, counting stock. Flat, exact, no adjectives. Headline: "CASH FOR / GOLD" — two lines, one sentence, Big Shoulders Stencil Display in ink on both, never a colour change on line two. Selling point: "TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU" plus "WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE". Money band: "PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE" — a number a seller can check, which is the whole point of not saying 'top prices'. Items: 10k • 14k • 18k • Scrap & Dental • Cuban Links • Rolex • Cartier • Tiffany • Yurman. Kicker: GOLD BUYER. Sticker: ON THE SPOT. Badges DISCREET / PRIVATE / LICENSED — never INSURED.
variations: Bars only — the twelve cells all gold-bars-* and gold-bar-single, which reads as a bullion inventory rather than a jewellery case
Jewellery case — chains, cuffs, rings and earrings only, no bars
Gold on aubergine (nn10) vs gold on violet (jw02) — same wall, the scrim hue is the only change
Kicker in Special Elite — one short word only, the typewriter the owner asked to keep, never on body copy
looks.collectionNote:
NIGHT COUNTER is the dark half of the library: ten cards you could tell from the other nine collections in a dark room, because every one of them is a lit object on a black counter and nothing else.

WHAT HOLDS THEM TOGETHER (five locks, all ten obey):
1. GROUND VALUE. Measured, not guessed: every palette here has a ground luminance under 0.06 — Jewel c1 sits at 0.046-0.057, Night Neon at 0.016-0.019. Nine palettes, five Jewel (jw01 jw02 jw05 jw07 jw09) and four Night Neon (nn01 nn02 nn09 nn10). Nothing else may enter.
2. ONE WARM LIGHT, USED ONCE. Every palette in the set answers its deep ground with a single warm-side accent — nn10 #f5ba08 gold, jw02 #fec674 amber, nn02 #feb263 amber, jw01 #fdc3a0 peach, jw09 #fdc0b7 coral, nn01 #fcaca5 peach. On the velvet/brushed grounds the light is physical (the radial lift); on tile, cast and photo it is the accent, and it may fill exactly ONE plate on the card. Two lit plates is the fault that turns this collection into an arcade.
3. STENCIL OR CONDENSED, ALWAYS. Display is drawn only from Big Shoulders Stencil Display, Big Shoulders Display, Oswald, Barlow Condensed, Saira Condensed, Teko — stencil scored 60% and condensed 49%, the top of the face data. Support is always a grotesque (56%). This also disables glow by interlock: DESIGN-LAW turns glow off on condensed faces, so no card in this collection can grow a neon halo. Monospace numerals (JetBrains Mono, DM Mono) appear only where the lead palette is Night Neon — the design law allows mono digits for Space, Night Neon and Liquid Glass only.
4. METAL AND GLASS ONLY. gold, silver, coins, phones. No cars, no cards, no strips, no Android, no watches (unpopular category), no Pokemon/sports slab frame — slabFrame() in retheme_lab.mjs is gated to /pokemon|sports/ anyway, and the owner set the slab rule explicitly.
5. NO CASH IN THE PICTURE. The cash is in the words (CASH FOR GOLD, PAID TODAY, ON THE SPOT); the picture stays the goods. cash-*, money-bag-sack, safe-open-cash and the cash ground (33%) are barred collection-wide. That is one fewer concept per card, which is the owner's actual complaint.

HOW YOU TELL IT FROM THE OTHER NINE: the other collections are lit from everywhere; this one is lit from one place. Four grounds only — tile x4, cast x3, deep x2, photo x1 — no scene, no slab, no paper, no abstract mesh/blobs/bokeh/confetti/skyline/waves/chevron/halftone. Six layouts only: reviewProof, stepsFlow, trustSeal, checklistHero, neonNight, arcCrown. Line-art marks only, never emoji, and never 'bolt' or 'burst' — the two marks that read arcade.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE BRIEF, both measured in the repo, both deliberate:
- INK POP IS NOT A DEEP FAMILY. ik01-ik10 c1 runs #e5f3f6 to #fbedea, luminance 0.865-0.878 — near-white. An Ink Pop card in this set would be a white card among nine black ones and would break the collection at a glance. Excluded.
- DUOTONE IS MID-TONE, NOT DEEP. du01-du10 c1 luminance runs 0.270-0.318; du08 Indigo Trade, the best of them at 44%, is #5593ef — a bright blue. Excluded for the same reason. Its approvals belong to a mid-tone collection, not this one.

THREE ENGINE FACTS THE SPECS ARE BUILT ON (read out of scripts/retheme_lab.mjs, not assumed):
- TILE on a deep palette does NOT paint the palette. `light = lum(c1)>0.55 ? c1 : lum(c2)>0.55 ? c2 : '#eceef2'` — both are deep here, so the lattice always lands on #eceef2 and then takes scrimColor = c1 at 0.6. The wall is a pale vitrine dimmed 60%: bright metal survives it, dark bodies do not. That is why the metals get the walls and why the phone wall is written around the cosmic-orange and silver bodies.
- CAST on a deep palette is exactly the collection's premise: ground c1, a white 0.10 diagonal lift, the hero at 62% width rotated -0.12 with a 40px shadow, then the window shadow at 0.5 and a c1 scrim at 0.22. It needs a hero cutout or it silently falls through to tile, so every cast theme's mustShow names its hero.
- BUSY PHOTOS on a deep palette take c1 at 0.44 (not 0.62 — that branch is for light grounds). A coin macro measures 37-47 on the detail scale, so the one photo theme here lands as a coin in a dark case, which is the only reason a 28%-approval ground earns a slot.

Also flagged, and enforced in neverShow across the metals: CATEGORY_COPY in retheme_lab.mjs still ships INSURED in the gold, silver and coins badge arrays, and the owner's standing rule is that INSURED is a car-buyer seal only — metals use DISCREET / PRIVATE / TRUSTED. And the silver deck's sub line names TEA SETS while silver-tea-set and silver-serving-tray are both rejected cutouts, so that line can never be backed by a picture; the silver themes prefer the two lines that can be.

looks.name: Cuban Cast
looks.oneLine: One Cuban link bracelet drawn huge into the ground under a single diagonal window shadow, the money word across the lit half.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: dg='cast', which requires a hero cutout — the theme is invalid without one. Ground fills jw02 c1=#3e3577, then a linear white 0.10 -> 0 from the top-left corner. The hero is fitted to 0.62W x 0.92H, translated to (0.66W, 0.52H), rotated -0.12 rad, drawn at alpha 0.92 with shadowColor rgba(0,0,0,0.35), blur 40, offset 24/30. Then the window shadow: a blurred (26px) rgba(8,10,16,0.5) wedge from 0.62W to the right edge, plus a 60px-blur penumbra at 0.25 from 0.5W. Finally scrimColor = c1 at 0.22. Because lum(jw02.c1)=0.049 the pale branch never runs — no ink body, no 0.58 shadow, no 0.30 scrim. The result is one object, one light from upper-left, one shadow falling right: the whole collection's thesis in a single card. Copy lives on the LIT left third; nothing sits over the bracelet. Panels over the cast go solid at rgba(c1,0.9) with white copy. The ONE lit plate is the CTA, in jw02 accent #fec674 (nn02 #feb263).
looks.imagery: Hero is HERO.gold[0] = gold-bracelet-cuban, the piece the owner put first. Alternates, in order: gold-watch-luxury, gold-chains-pile, gold-necklace-single, gold-class-ring, gold-bracelet-pair. Note gold-nuggets-raw is HERO.gold[3] in the engine but is a REJECTED cutout (off-category) and is filtered by okCut — if it ever renders, the card is invalid. No second product. Marks: at most two line-art gold marks (chain, ingot), flanking the money word at the 118px clearance, never touching it.
looks.copy: The written-offer voice: we test it, you watch, you decide. Headline: "CASH OUT YOUR / GOLD" — the METAL opener rotation the engine already carries for gold, one face and one colour across both lines. Selling point: "WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE" plus "TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU". Money band: "PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE". CTA: GET A FREE QUOTE. Challenge variant names only household targets — WE BEAT / CASH4GOLD or WE TOP / THE PAWN SHOP; never a bare WE MATCH without an object.
variations: Bracelet lead (default) vs president-watch lead — gold-watch-luxury is the only watch permitted anywhere in this collection, and only as the gold hero, never as a watch-category card
Shadow left — mirror the wedge so the light falls from the right; use on one card in three so a page of these is not all the same diagonal
Amber on violet (jw02) vs amber on near-black violet (nn02) — nn02's deeper ground makes the bracelet the only bright object on the card
Challenge cut — WE BEAT / CASH4GOLD replaces the opener, items line unchanged

looks.name: Under One Lamp
looks.oneLine: A jeweller's scale with gold in the pan, sitting in a soft pool of light on black velvet that falls away to nothing at the edges.
looks.groundSpec: Engine ground kind = 'velvet' (grounds.js K.velvet, owner-ticked, 5 kinds ticks). Because dark(P) is true for nn10 (lum 0.016 < 0.35) it fills c1 #2c1c37 directly, then a radial from centre: rgba(#ffffff,0.12) at the middle out to rgba(0,0,0,0.35) at 0.75W, then film grain at 0.08. velvet is in the no-extra-grain list so it does not get the usual 0.05 pass on top. This is the literal 'one warm light' of the collection: a lit centre, black corners, cloth texture. Force it with LAB_GROUNDS=velvet or LAB_ABS=1 — the look-ground hook in retheme_lab.mjs currently honours only 'cast' and 'tile', so a velvet theme must be pinned rather than requested. SPOTLIGHT IS FORBIDDEN as the substitute: it is on the owner's `never` list in approved-grounds.json alongside marble, memphis and linen. Fallbacks in order if velvet is unavailable: vignetteG (linear c1->c2 plus a 0.45 vignette) then glow (accent radial 0.55 at 0.38H). The hero sits in the lit centre; copy sits above and below it in the falloff. On nn02 the same build runs on #241f3b with #feb263 as the accent. Exactly one plate lit: the money band.
looks.imagery: Hero is gold-scale-weighing — the only asset in the library that pictures the sentence TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU, which is why this theme exists. Second object, optional and small, in the falloff: gold-scrap-mixed or gold-rings-scatter (what is being weighed), never touching the hero and never over text. Alternates for the hero: gold-jewelry-mixed, gold-earrings-pile. Marks: one line-art gem or ingot, one corner, no emoji.
looks.copy: The estate appraisal: quiet, private, unhurried — the opposite of a gold-party ad. Headline: "CASH IN YOUR / GOLD". Selling point: "ESTATES HANDLED DISCREETLY" plus "TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU" — the second line is the picture, which is the whole reason the scale is the hero. Money band: "PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE". CTA: GET A FREE QUOTE. Kicker: GOLD BUYER. Trust line: SINCE 2015. Badges DISCREET / PRIVATE — never INSURED.
variations: Scale alone in the light — no second object, the emptiest card in the collection and the one that proves the ground
Scale plus scrap in the falloff — gold-scrap-mixed at 260px, well clear of every text box
Vignette build (vignetteG) instead of velvet — a linear c1->c2 with 0.45 dark edges, for runs where velvet cannot be pinned
Gold light on aubergine (nn10) vs amber light on violet (nn02)

looks.name: Sterling Drawer
looks.oneLine: A canteen drawer pulled open after closing: eleven pieces of sterling — flatware, rounds, bars, candlesticks — laid in an even lattice under petrol blue.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: dg='tile'. jw09 c1=#054666 (lum 0.054) and c2=#023153 are both deep, so the 4x3 lattice lands on the hard-coded #eceef2 with 28px gaps and 242x322 cells, cutouts at 0.96 with rgba(0,0,0,0.28) shadows (blur 26, offset 10/16), then scrimColor = c1 at 0.6. Silver is the ideal wall subject: it is the brightest family in the cutout library, so it survives the 60% dim where a dark body would not. The silver pool holds 11 approved items against 12 cells, so exactly one piece repeats — acceptable in a lattice, and the repeat should be a bar or a rounds pile, never a distinctive silhouette like the candlesticks. Panels over the wall go solid at rgba(#054666,0.9), copy #ffffff. ONE lit plate: the money band in jw09 accent #fdc0b7 — a warm coral light over cold metal, which is the reason this palette is here rather than a cool-accent one. jw09's cyan support #3ebfc9 may appear as a hairline rule only; as a plate fill it makes a second light and breaks the family.
looks.imagery: The full approved silver pool, twelve cells from eleven pieces: silver-flatware-set, silver-flatware, silver-rounds-pile, silver-bars-stack, silver-bars-row, silver-bars, silver-bar-single, silver-coins-spill, silver-coins-tube, silver-candlesticks, silver-jewelry-mixed. No hero on top of the wall. Marks: line art from the silver set (gem, ringMark, chain, ingot), two maximum, corners only.
looks.copy: The estate voice again, but colder — sterling is inherited, not bought. Headline: "WE BUY / SILVER". Selling point: "WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU, SPOT SHOWN" plus "ANTIQUE AND ESTATE PIECES WELCOME". Money band: "PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE". Items: Sterling • .925 • Silverware • Antiques • Tiffany & Co • David Yurman • Chrome Hearts. CTA: GET A FREE QUOTE. NOTE: the silver deck's third sub line ends '...TEA SETS', and both silver-tea-set and silver-serving-tray are rejected cutouts — that line can never be backed by a picture on this card, so this theme uses the other two.
variations: Flatware drawer — the wall built from silver-flatware, silver-flatware-set, silver-coins-spill and the bars, no jewellery
Bullion drawer — bars, rounds and coin tubes only, which pairs with the SPOT line
Candlestick corner — silver-candlesticks placed in one corner cell only, never repeated across the lattice
Coral light (jw09) vs pink light (jw05) — jw05 is the cooler ground; its mint support #56c1a1 is hairlines only

looks.name: Under The Loupe
looks.oneLine: A Morgan dollar macro sunk into deep indigo at 44% — the only photograph in the collection, used because the photograph is genuinely the thing the headline names.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: the WEBBG branch, bgcat='coins'. On jw01 (c1=#1f3e7a, lum 0.051) every busy coin macro takes scrimColor = c1 at 0.44 — NOT 0.62, because that branch is gated on lum(c1) >= 0.25 and this ground is far below it. Measured detail scores from backdrop-lum.json: coins-american-gold-eagle-coin-1 (46.62), coins-morgan-silver-dollar-3 (46.57), coins-american-gold-eagle-coin-2 (37.76), coins-morgan-silver-dollar-1 (18.55) are all past the busy threshold of 14 and take the 0.44 palette tint. The three quieter shots — coins-coin-collection-album-1 (13.09), coins-morgan-silver-dollar-2 (12.99), coins-american-gold-eagle-coin-3 (8.67) — fall to the c1/c2 branch at 0.40+gap (clamped 0.42-0.68) or the accent branch at 0.30. All of those land dark; none of them lands pale. HARD RULE: the photograph must carry a palette tint. The engine's `raw` pass (sd%4===2, non-busy only) and the `natural` pass (sd%3===1) substitute a neutral #000000 scrim at 0.36/0.46 and drop the palette — on this theme those treatments are invalid and the card is rejected. This is the collection's one concession to a 28%-approval ground, and it is earned only because a coin macro IS the subject: on any other category this ground would be barred.

looks.collectionNote:
NIGHT COUNTER is the dark half of the library: ten cards you could tell from the other nine collections in a dark room, because every one of them is a lit object on a black counter and nothing else.

WHAT HOLDS THEM TOGETHER (five locks, all ten obey):
1. GROUND VALUE. Measured, not guessed: every palette here has a ground luminance under 0.06 — Jewel c1 sits at 0.046-0.057, Night Neon at 0.016-0.019. Nine palettes, five Jewel (jw01 jw02 jw05 jw07 jw09) and four Night Neon (nn01 nn02 nn09 nn10). Nothing else may enter.
2. ONE WARM LIGHT, USED ONCE. Every palette in the set answers its deep ground with a single warm-side accent — nn10 #f5ba08 gold, jw02 #fec674 amber, nn02 #feb263 amber, jw01 #fdc3a0 peach, jw09 #fdc0b7 coral, nn01 #fcaca5 peach. On the velvet/brushed grounds the light is physical (the radial lift); on tile, cast and photo it is the accent, and it may fill exactly ONE plate on the card. Two lit plates is the fault that turns this collection into an arcade.
3. STENCIL OR CONDENSED, ALWAYS. Display is drawn only from Big Shoulders Stencil Display, Big Shoulders Display, Oswald, Barlow Condensed, Saira Condensed, Teko — stencil scored 60% and condensed 49%, the top of the face data. Support is always a grotesque (56%). This also disables glow by interlock: DESIGN-LAW turns glow off on condensed faces, so no card in this collection can grow a neon halo. Monospace numerals (JetBrains Mono, DM Mono) appear only where the lead palette is Night Neon — the design law allows mono digits for Space, Night Neon and Liquid Glass only.
4. METAL AND GLASS ONLY. gold, silver, coins, phones. No cars, no cards, no strips, no Android, no watches (unpopular category), no Pokemon/sports slab frame — slabFrame() in retheme_lab.mjs is gated to /pokemon|sports/ anyway, and the owner set the slab rule explicitly.
5. NO CASH IN THE PICTURE. The cash is in the words (CASH FOR GOLD, PAID TODAY, ON THE SPOT); the picture stays the goods. cash-*, money-bag-sack, safe-open-cash and the cash ground (33%) are barred collection-wide. That is one fewer concept per card, which is the owner's actual complaint.

HOW YOU TELL IT FROM THE OTHER NINE: the other collections are lit from everywhere; this one is lit from one place. Four grounds only — tile x4, cast x3, deep x2, photo x1 — no scene, no slab, no paper, no abstract mesh/blobs/bokeh/confetti/skyline/waves/chevron/halftone. Six layouts only: reviewProof, stepsFlow, trustSeal, checklistHero, neonNight, arcCrown. Line-art marks only, never emoji, and never 'bolt' or 'burst' — the two marks that read arcade.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE BRIEF, both measured in the repo, both deliberate:
- INK POP IS NOT A DEEP FAMILY. ik01-ik10 c1 runs #e5f3f6 to #fbedea, luminance 0.865-0.878 — near-white. An Ink Pop card in this set would be a white card among nine black ones and would break the collection at a glance. Excluded.
- DUOTONE IS MID-TONE, NOT DEEP. du01-du10 c1 luminance runs 0.270-0.318; du08 Indigo Trade, the best of them at 44%, is #5593ef — a bright blue. Excluded for the same reason. Its approvals belong to a mid-tone collection, not this one.

THREE ENGINE FACTS THE SPECS ARE BUILT ON (read out of scripts/retheme_lab.mjs, not assumed):
- TILE on a deep palette does NOT paint the palette. `light = lum(c1)>0.55 ? c1 : lum(c2)>0.55 ? c2 : '#eceef2'` — both are deep here, so the lattice always lands on #eceef2 and then takes scrimColor = c1 at 0.6. The wall is a pale vitrine dimmed 60%: bright metal survives it, dark bodies do not. That is why the metals get the walls and why the phone wall is written around the cosmic-orange and silver bodies.
- CAST on a deep palette is exactly the collection's premise: ground c1, a white 0.10 diagonal lift, the hero at 62% width rotated -0.12 with a 40px shadow, then the window shadow at 0.5 and a c1 scrim at 0.22. It needs a hero cutout or it silently falls through to tile, so every cast theme's mustShow names its hero.
- BUSY PHOTOS on a deep palette take c1 at 0.44 (not 0.62 — that branch is for light grounds). A coin macro measures 37-47 on the detail scale, so the one photo theme here lands as a coin in a dark case, which is the only reason a 28%-approval ground earns a slot.

Also flagged, and enforced in neverShow across the metals: CATEGORY_COPY in retheme_lab.mjs still ships INSURED in the gold, silver and coins badge arrays, and the owner's standing rule is that INSURED is a car-buyer seal only — metals use DISCREET / PRIVATE / TRUSTED. And the silver deck's sub line names TEA SETS while silver-tea-set and silver-serving-tray are both rejected cutouts, so that line can never be backed by a picture; the silver themes prefer the two lines that can be.

looks.name: Cosmic Orange Counter
looks.oneLine: The cosmic orange iPhone 17 Pro cast into deep indigo at two-thirds width with the window shadow across it — the shop's money-maker, lit like a piece of jewellery.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: dg='cast', hero required. Ground fills jw01 c1=#1f3e7a (lum 0.051), white 0.10 -> 0 from top-left, hero at 0.62W x 0.92H, translated (0.66W, 0.52H), rotated -0.12, alpha 0.92, shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.35) blur 40 offset 24/30; window shadow blurred 26px rgba(8,10,16,0.5) from 0.62W plus a 60px penumbra at 0.25; scrim c1 at 0.22. The pale branch cannot fire. This is the one card in the set where the SUBJECT is the warm light: the cosmic orange body against deep indigo is a warm object on a cold ground, so the accent plate should be small — the CTA only, in jw01 accent #fdc3a0, which is a peach a half-step off the phone's own orange rather than a competing hue. On nn02 the ground goes near-black violet #241f3b and the amber accent #feb263 pulls toward the phone; keep the accent to one plate there too. Panels over the cast go solid at rgba(c1,0.9) with white copy.
looks.imagery: Hero: own-apple-cosmic-orange-16, -20, -07, -02, -03, -06, -10 — Apple's own press renders of the current iPhone, single units, the deck's first cut. Silver alternates: own-apple-silver-11, own-apple-silver-15. Cool alternates: own-apple-deep-blue-09, own-apple-deep-blue-18 — usable here (the cast keeps its own highlight) though they lose the warm-object idea. The qs-iphone-* press files are TWO-UP COMPOSITES — a back and a front overlapping in one file — so they are barred across both phone themes in this collection, and so are the ip-group-* multi-unit shots and the in-hand shots. No ip-gen* asset may ever be named: ip-gen17-plateau-black, -blue, -white and ip-gen15-pro-back-natural appear in the approved list but are AI-generated fake iPhones and are excluded by the LEGACY regex in retheme_lab.mjs. Marks: one line-art phoneMark or check, one corner — never a bolt, never an emoji.
looks.copy: The buyer who already knows what your phone is worth. Headline: "SELL YOUR / iPHONE" — one face, one colour, both lines. Selling point: "SAME-DAY PAYMENT, EVERY TIME" plus "WE MEET YOU LOCALLY OR YOU MAIL IT IN". Money band: "UP TO $1,100 PAID TODAY", money word $1,100 — bounded, checkable. Items: iPhone 17 • 16 • 15 • Pro & Pro Max. Kicker: APPLE BUYER. CTA: GET YOUR OFFER. Cities: LONG BEACH · LAKEWOOD · DOWNEY · CARSON · TORRANCE. Challenge cut names household buyers only — WE BEAT / ECOATM, WE TOP / GAZELLE, WE BEAT / BEST BUY. AUDIT INTERLOCK: the items line names iPhone 17 / 16 / 15, so the hero must be a current body — iPhone 12 is the floor and every pre-12 cutout is out. On neonNight the display face is condensed, so the layout's glow is disabled by the design law; the card keeps the structure and loses the halo.
variations: Cosmic orange lead (default) — the warm object on the cold ground, the reference build
Silver lead — own-apple-silver-11, which turns the card monochrome and lets the accent plate do all the warming
Shadow left — mirror the wedge, one card in three

looks.name: Closing Time Wall
looks.oneLine: The device wall from the shop's own site, after hours: twelve single iPhones in an even lattice, dimmed sixty percent into indigo, with the opening hours running under the money band.
looks.groundSpec: Engine path: dg='tile'. jw09 c1=#054666 (lum 0.054) and c2=#023153 are both deep, so the lattice lands on the hard-coded #eceef2: 4x3, 28px gaps, 242x322 cells, cutouts fitted at 0.96 with rgba(0,0,0,0.28) shadows (blur 26, offset 10/16), then scrimColor = c1 at 0.6. THIS IS THE THEME'S RISK AND ITS RULE: at 60% dim, a wall of dark phone bodies goes to mush. The pool must therefore be weighted to bright bodies — at least six of the twelve cells must be a cosmic-orange or silver unit. The eleven approved own-apple singles fill twelve cells with exactly one repeat; that repeat must be an orange unit, never a deep-blue one. Panels over the wall go solid at rgba(#054666,0.9) with #ffffff copy, which is what keeps UP TO $1,100 PAID TODAY off the lattice. ONE lit plate: the money band in jw09 accent #fdc0b7. The cyan support #3ebfc9 is hairlines only.
looks.imagery: Twelve cells from the eleven approved own-apple singles: own-apple-cosmic-orange-02, -03, -06, -07, -10, -16, -20, own-apple-silver-11, own-apple-silver-15, own-apple-deep-blue-09, own-apple-deep-blue-18. These are single units, which is the whole reason the wall works — every cell holds one object. The qs-iphone-* files are two-up composites (a back and a front overlapping) and would put two devices in one cell, so they are barred; so are ip-group-*, qs-set-*, the pair and lineup shots, and every in-hand shot. iphone-17-pro-back-black and iphone-17-pro-back-silver are approved singles and may substitute. No ip-gen* asset ever: the four ip-gen entries in the approved list are AI-generated fake iPhones, ticked at thumbnail size by mistake and excluded by the LEGACY regex. No hero on top of the wall. Marks: one line-art check or phoneMark, corner.
looks.copy: The shop itself, not a pitch — this is what is on the counter tonight. Headline: "SELL YOUR / iPHONE". Selling point: "CRACKED, LOCKED OR BLACKLISTED" plus "SAME-DAY PAYMENT, EVERY TIME". Money band: "UP TO $1,100 PAID TODAY". Hours line carries the theme's name: OPEN 7 DAYS · 9AM-8PM · WALK-INS WELCOME. Items: iPhone 17 • 16 • 15 • Pro & Pro Max. Kicker: APPLE BUYER. CTA: GET YOUR OFFER. Payment line: CASH · ZELLE · VENMO · WIRE — YOUR CHOICE. Sticker: PAID TODAY. AUDIT INTERLOCK: CRACKED, LOCKED OR BLACKLISTED is a copy claim, not a picture — the wall stays clean units, because the owner's rejection list bars heavy damage imagery outright (it reads as a repair ad).
variations: Orange wall — nine or more of the twelve cells cosmic orange, which makes the lattice itself the warm light and lets the accent plate drop out
Two-tone wall — orange and silver only, no deep blue, the highest-contrast build under the 60% dim
Petrol (jw09) vs indigo (jw01) — the same lattice, the scrim hue is the only change
Hours-led — the opening-hours line promoted above the money band on stepsFlow, one card in three

looks.name: Blue Pen Estimate
looks.oneLine: A cream ruled sheet with three punch holes down the left, a typed estimate in navy ballpoint, one yellow highlighter across the money line, and a single iPhone laid on the page with its own shadow.
looks.groundSpec: Pin the sheet to paper:ruled — #fbf7ea stock, 2.2px #9fb9df rules every 54px from y=150, a 2.2px #e08f8f margin rule at x=118, three punched holes down the left at 18/50/82% of height (a 15r #eef0f2 disc over a 0.10 black shadow disc), 9000 two-pixel fibre specks up to 0.035 alpha, and a 70px rgba(0,0,0,0.10)→0 binding shadow along the top edge. Painted as bg {type:'image', src:'paper:ruled', scrimColor: th.c1, scrim: 0.001} — the scrim is nominal so the palette NEVER tints the paper. The engine today rotates the four stocks on seed%5; this look pins ruled. Sheen, Vignette and Grain layers go to opacity 0. Highlighter: exactly one stroke, HIGHLIGHT pastel at 0.55 opacity, rx = 0.18 x height, angle ±0.8°, with its Marker Overrun twin beneath (same fill, 0.30 opacity, +22px wide, −10px left, +3px top, angle −0.6°) so the ends run past the words. Panels become sticky notes: STICKY pastel at 0.96, rx 4, tilt ±1.2°, shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.22) blur 22 offset 4/10. Squares under 130px become solid pen boxes, rx 8, angle 0, numerals white. Headline and phone number take the pen (#084f88 on lp01, #0c42ab on lp08); kicker, sub, items, CTA, badges and website all take #26231f. Single-line copy snaps its baseline to the 54px rule grid, row type stays under 40px so it sits between the rules. PALE VS DEEP: every palette here is pale (c1 #ecf4fd, L 0.95) and the sheet is drawn rather than derived, so a pale palette changes nothing — the stock is the stock. If a deep palette were ever substituted the rule holds: the sheet keeps its own colour, the pen takes th.accent only, the ink stays #26231f, and the sheet is never inverted to a dark ground.
looks.imagery: One Apple unit, never a pile, sitting lower-right clear of every line of type, with a real cast shadow onto the sheet. iPhone cards lead with own-apple-cosmic-orange-10 (the orange 17 Pro Max the owner calls the money maker), then own-apple-cosmic-orange-02, own-apple-deep-blue-09, own-apple-silver-11, iphone-17-pro-back-black, iphone-17-pro-back-silver, qs-iphone-17-pro-max, qs-iphone-16-pro. iPad cards take qs-ipad-pro-13-m5, qs-ipad-air-11-m3, qs-ipad-mini-7-a17-pro or ipad-with-pencil. MacBook cards take qs-device-macbook-pro, own-stock-macbook-open or mac-pro-open-front. One or two pen-drawn marks only (phoneMark, bolt, check, dollar) in free corners, in th.accent and th.ink, never in the middle of the card and never as emoji.
neverShow: an iPad or a Mac on a card whose headline says iPHONE (and the reverse)
handwriting faces (Permanent Marker, Kalam, Patrick Hand, Shadows Into Light, Gloria Hallelujah, Nanum Pen Script, Architects Daughter, Amatic SC, Cabin Sketch)

looks.collectionNote: Ten cards that are all the same physical object: a sheet of real stationery with an offer written out on it. The ground is never a photograph and never a gradient — it is one of the four drawn stocks in retheme_lab.mjs (paper:ruled cream #fbf7ea, paper:legal canary #fff3b8, paper:grid cool #f7f9fb, paper:dots warm #fbfaf5), each with its fibre noise, its 70px binding shadow across the top and, on ruled and legal, its red margin rule at x=118. Every palette is a Lined Paper (lp) theme, which means one thing only: the palette IS THE PEN. th.accent is a single deep ink at L≈0.42 — navy, royal blue, teal, pine, grass, violet, magenta, oxblood, crimson, signal red — and nothing else on the card is coloured except one translucent highlighter stroke with overrun ends and, where a layout has a panel, one sticky note. All body copy is PRINTED type from assets/approved-fonts.json, never a handwriting face: the engine's Lined Paper default sets the whole card in Kalam and Patrick Hand, and every theme here overrides it through look.faces because the brief is an offer TYPED OUT for the customer, not a doodle. What separates this collection from the other nine at a glance: no photograph anywhere, no abstract ground, no device wall, no glass, no neon, no gradient, no emoji — a white or cream page with ruled lines, a single ink, one marker stroke, and one product photographed as if laid on the page with its own drop shadow. Pokémon is deliberately absent: the owner's own PALFIT rule in retheme_lab.mjs reads pokemon avoid /Paper|Pastel/, and pokemon has exactly one approved cutout (poke-slabs-trio), so the collection covers sports cards instead. Watches are absent by the owner's rule. Bikes appear only as a variation on the tow sheet, never as a theme.

looks.name: Legal Pad Payout
looks.oneLine: Canary legal-pad stock with navy ballpoint and a wide highlighter band under the spot line, cool grey silver laid on the yellow page so the metal reads.
looks.groundSpec: Pin the sheet to paper:legal — #fff3b8 canary stock, 2.2px #8fabd6 rules every 54px from y=130, a 2.2px #d97f7f margin rule at x=118, NO punch holes (a legal pad is glued at the head, not punched), fibre noise as above, 70px rgba(0,0,0,0.10)→0 binding shadow at the top. bg {type:'image', src:'paper:legal', scrimColor: th.c1, scrim: 0.001}: the canary is the canary, the palette never tints it. Sheen, Vignette and Grain to opacity 0. The highlighter is the hero here because bandKnockout gives it a full-width band: one stroke, 0.55 opacity, rx 0.18 x height, angle ±0.8°, with the Marker Overrun twin at 0.30 opacity running 22px past each end. Panels become one sticky note only, 0.96 opacity, tilt ±1.2°, drop shadow blur 22 offset 4/10. Squares under 130px become solid navy pen boxes with white numerals. Pen #0c42ab (lp08) or #084f88 (lp01) carries the headline and the phone number; everything else is #26231f. Baselines snap to the 54px grid from y=130; row type under 40px. PALE VS DEEP: both palettes are pale (c1 #eef4fe / #ecf4fd) and the canary is drawn, not derived — nothing about the stock moves with the palette. A deep palette would still leave the sheet canary and only darken the pen; the sheet is never inverted.
looks.imagery: Cool grey silver against warm canary is the whole point of pairing this stock with this category. Hero silver-flatware-set or silver-rounds-pile, then silver-bars-stack, silver-bars-row, silver-bar-single, silver-coins-spill, silver-coins-tube, silver-jewelry-mixed, silver-candlesticks, silver-flatware. One object, laid flat on the page, lower right or lower left, with its own drop shadow, clear of the type. Marks are the silver set drawn in pen: gem, sparkle, coin, ingot, ringMark — one or two, corners only.
neverShow: handwriting faces (Permanent Marker, Kalam, Patrick Hand, Shadows Into Light, Gloria Hallelujah, Nanum Pen Script, Architects Daughter, Amatic SC, Cabin Sketch)

looks.name: Graph Paper Quote
looks.oneLine: An engineer's grid sheet in cool white with a deep teal technical pen, prices set in DM Mono and squared to the 48px lattice, one Mac or iPad laid on the grid.
looks.groundSpec: Pin the sheet to paper:grid — #f7f9fb cool stock with a 1.4px #b9cbe2 lattice every 48px in both axes, no margin rule, no punch holes, the same 9000-speck fibre noise and the same 70px rgba(0,0,0,0.10)→0 top shadow. bg {type:'image', src:'paper:grid', scrimColor: th.c1, scrim: 0.001}. Sheen, Vignette and Grain to opacity 0. Because there are no horizontal rules to snap to, the 48px lattice does the aligning: the money figure and every number in the ladder sit on a lattice line, and stepsFlow's numbered squares are drawn one full lattice cell wide so the boxes land on the grid instead of floating over it. Pen boxes: squares under 130px take #06585c at full opacity, rx 8, angle 0, numerals white. One highlighter only, 0.55 opacity, rx 0.18 x height, angle ±0.8°, Marker Overrun twin at 0.30 opacity 22px longer — on grid stock the overrun is what stops the stroke reading as a printed rectangle. One sticky note maximum, 0.96 opacity, tilt ±1.2°, shadow blur 22 offset 4/10. Headline and phone number in #06585c; all other copy #26231f. PALE VS DEEP: lp05's c1 is #e9f7f7, L 0.95 — pale, and irrelevant, because the grid stock is drawn. A deep palette would still leave the sheet cool white; only the pen darkens, and the lattice colour never changes.
looks.imagery: One machine, flat on the grid, lower right, clear of the type, with a real drop shadow. Mac cards: qs-device-macbook-pro, qs-device-macbook-air, own-stock-macbook-open, own-stock-macbook-stack, mac-pro-open-front, mac-half-open-glow, mac-pair-open-angle. iPad cards: qs-ipad-pro-13-m5, qs-ipad-pro-11-m5, qs-ipad-air-13-m3, qs-ipad-air-11-m3, qs-ipad-mini-7-a17-pro, ipad-with-pencil, ipad-with-keyboard. looks.name: Dotted Appraisal Note
looks.oneLine: A warm dot-grid page written in crimson with an Instrument Serif hand, a Cuban bracelet and the weighing scale laid on the paper, sealed like a jeweller's appraisal.
looks.groundSpec: Pin the sheet to paper:dots — #fbfaf5 warm stock with 2.2r #b3bbc7 dots on a 44px pitch starting at x=30,y=30, no rules, no margin, no punch holes, the same fibre noise and the same 70px rgba(0,0,0,0.10)→0 top shadow. bg {type:'image', src:'paper:dots', scrimColor: th.c1, scrim: 0.001}. Sheen, Vignette and Grain to opacity 0. The dots are neutral grey, which is why gold sits on this stock and not on the canary legal pad — warm white plus grey dots leaves the yellow metal the only warm thing in the frame. trustSeal leads, so the seal reads as the appraiser's stamp: keep it a hairline circle in the pen (#90043c), never a glass badge, never a gradient medal. One highlighter only, 0.55 opacity, rx 0.18 x height, angle ±0.8°, with the Marker Overrun twin at 0.30 opacity 22px longer. One sticky note maximum, 0.96 opacity, tilt ±1.2°, shadow blur 22 offset 4/10. Headline and phone number in #90043c; the rest #26231f. There are no rules on dot stock, so the baseline snap is off and the type is set on a 44px vertical rhythm instead. PALE VS DEEP: lp10's c1 is #fdf0f1, L 0.95, and it never reaches the paper — the stock is drawn. A deep palette would still leave the page warm white and only deepen the pen.
looks.imagery: Jewellery, one piece at a time, laid on the page with a real cast shadow, lower right, clear of every line. Hero gold-bracelet-cuban, then gold-watch-luxury, gold-chains-pile, gold-necklace-single, gold-bracelet-pair, gold-class-ring, gold-rings-scatter, gold-earrings-pile, gold-jewelry-mixed. The scale variation uses gold-scale-weighing as the hero because the copy promises weighing in front of you and the picture should show it. Marks are the gold set in pen — gem, ringMark, chain, sparkle, coin — one or two, corners only, never gold-coloured (on this family the marks take th.accent and th.ink, not the gold swatches).

looks.name: Red Pen Tow Sheet
looks.oneLine: A cream ruled sheet marked up in signal red, one wide highlighter under the cash figure, keys and a vehicle on the page, and the make's own wordmark inked in the corner when the headline names one.
looks.groundSpec: Pin the sheet to paper:ruled — #fbf7ea, 2.2px #9fb9df rules every 54px from y=150, 2.2px #e08f8f margin rule at x=118, three punched holes at 18/50/82% down the left, fibre noise, 70px top binding shadow. bg {type:'image', src:'paper:ruled', scrimColor: th.c1, scrim: 0.001}. Sheen, Vignette and Grain to opacity 0. bandKnockout leads so the highlighter is the loudest object on the card: one stroke at 0.55 opacity across the cash figure, rx 0.18 x height, angle ±0.8°, with the Marker Overrun twin at 0.30 opacity, +22px wide, −10px left, angle −0.6° — uneven ends are mandatory, a clean rectangle reads as a printed band and breaks the premise. One sticky note maximum. Squares under 130px become solid #920c03 pen boxes with white numerals. Headline and phone number in #920c03; everything else #26231f. Baselines snap to the 54px rule grid; row type under 40px. Brand cards: when the headline word is TOYOTAS, HONDAS, FORDS, CHEVYS, SILVERADOS, TACOMAS, TUNDRAS, F-150S, TRANSITS, NISSANS, JEEPS, TESLAS, BMWS, MERCEDES, SPRINTERS, HYUNDAIS, KIAS, DODGES, RAMS, HARLEYS, YAMAHAS or KAWASAKIS, that make's PNG from assets/logos is re-inked to #26231f and placed in the best free corner before any decorative mark. PALE VS DEEP: lp07's c1 is #fdf0ee, L 0.95, and never touches the sheet. A deep palette would leave the cream cream and only darken the pen.
looks.imagery: One vehicle or one set of keys, on the page, lower right, clear of the copy, with a real drop shadow. Cars: car-keys-fob, car-hand-keys-over, car-sedan-front, car-suv-side, car-front, car-sedan-rear, car-wheel-tyre, car-engine-bay, car-damaged-front (running or not is in the copy, so light damage is honest here). Trucks: car-truck-front. Vans: car-van-cargo. Bikes: car-motorcycle-side only. On a brand-led card the ONLY brand image is the inked wordmark — there is no per-make photography in the library, so the vehicle cutout stays generic and the wordmark does the naming. Marks are the cars/trucks/vans/bikes sets in pen: car, key, wheel, keyfob, flag, truck, van.

looks.name: Cosmic Orange Room
looks.oneLine: The Cosmic Orange 17 Pro and its copper set pieces held large in a deep teal room, a blind falling across the whole arrangement, SELL YOUR iPHONE stacked in the lit upper-left corner.
looks.groundSpec: DEEP BRANCH ONLY. jw05 c1 #044a51 (luminance 0.055) and jw06 c1 #014c44 (0.056) are far below the 0.55 pale threshold, so drawGround fills flat c1, lays a white diagonal sheen from 0.12 alpha at the top-left corner to zero at 55% across, draws the hero at min(0.62W/w, 0.92H/h) centred on 0.66W/0.52H at -0.12 rad with a black 0.35 shadow (blur 40, offset 24/30), then the window: blur-26 parallelogram at 0.50 with its top edge at 0.62W and its bottom edge at 0.22W, plus a blur-60 penumbra at 0.25. Scrim is c1 itself at 0.22 — the room stays a saturated teal, no ink veil, no grey, ever. The hero's own copper spheres and ribbons are the only warm thing in the frame; that is the whole picture idea, orange object against its split-complement. jw05's accent #febbd3 and jw06's #fdb6f2 carry the price plate and the sticker; the trust panel goes solid at rgba(#044a51, 0.9) with white copy. IF A WARM PALETTE IS EVER SUBSTITUTED the card collapses to orange-on-orange mud, which is the owner's banned dark-orange card — so the palette list is closed.

looks.collectionNote:
WINDOW LIGHT is ten cards that each hold ONE object in a coloured room with a blind drawn across it. The engine's `cast` ground is the whole identity: the product is painted into the background itself (retheme_lab.mjs line 3374 strips every Hero/Lineup product layer once __castBg is set), scaled to min(0.62W/w, 0.92H/h), centred at 0.66W/0.52H, rotated -0.12 rad, alpha 0.92, with a real contact shadow (blur 40, offset 24/30, black at 0.35); then two blurred parallelograms fall across it — blur 26 at full strength with its top edge at 0.62W and its bottom edge at 0.22W, and a blur-60 penumbra at half — so the light rakes from upper-left to lower-right and the copy always lives in the lit upper-left quadrant while the object fills the shadowed right two-thirds. Panels go solid over a cast ground, so every card in the family is the same two things: one lit object, one solid card of facts. You can tell this collection from the other nine at a glance because nothing is tiled, nothing is repeated, nothing overlaps, and there is exactly one product per card at three-quarter scale.

THE PALE-GREY PROBLEM, SOLVED BY A RULE, NOT BY HOPE. On a pale palette (relative luminance of c1 > 0.55) the cast branch repaints the room: c1, then th.ink at 0.20, then a vertical gradient of th.accent 0.18 to th.ink 0.10, then a scrim of th.ink at 0.30. Roughly half the finished ground is the INK colour. So on cast you choose a pale palette by its ink, never by its ground — and the ink must be cool. Programmable form: reject any pale palette whose ink red channel is not at least 16 below its blue channel. That single test passes pa05 (#1b4037), ca07 (#173f3f), ca01 (#183f3c), cd06 (#1b3d49), cd04 (#263f2b) and rejects every warm-inked pale palette — pp02 (#4a3220, +42), pp01, su01-su10, io04, gl02, ck02 — which are exactly the ones that turn taupe and land on the owner's banned "dark orange or brown". pp04 fails at +9, which is why the 62%-scoring Mint Counter Paper is NOT in this collection despite its score. Seven of the ten sit on deep palettes where the branch never veils at all (ground stays c1, sheen 0.10, scrim 0.22 of c1) and the room keeps full chroma; two and a half are the daylight members, drawn only from the cool-inked pale winners.

WHAT THE AUDIT THREW OUT, WITH REASONS I VERIFIED BY OPENING THE FILES. A cast hero is drawn 670px wide, so every fault is at maximum size. poke-slabs-trio is three EMPTY slabs with blank pastel faces and blank label strips — it is the only approved poke- cutout, so this collection has NO Pokémon theme and says so rather than shipping a giant blank. sports-slabs-stack and sports-slabs-fan-five are four and five blank slabs; only sports-slab has a real card face. silver-bars-stack shows silver-coloured bars stamped GOLD; silver-bars-row is stamped "WILD BOLD / 69906"; silver-rounds-pile carries Bitcoin symbols and "UNITED SATES OF AMERICA" — so the silver theme is sterling and silverware, not bullion. coin-graded-fan-three reads "V LODS OF EY / INO COH WO ROUT". strip-boxes-fan is a lateral-flow C/T/S cassette, the same not-diabetes fault the owner rejected strip-vials-pile for; strip-boxes-pile-large is plain kraft cartons. own-stock-macbook-open is a Touch Bar keyboard shot — a relic body and no screen. Every own-apple-* file is the same Cosmic Orange 17 Pro set regardless of "deep-blue" or "silver" in its name, so that theme owns the orange instead of pretending to a colour range. And the qs-* press renders are 400-500px two-up composites: fine small, unusable at 670px. None of these are in any mustShow; all are in the neverShow lists.

looks.name: Titanium Daylight
looks.oneLine: A black or white iPhone lying in a cool daylight room with the blind across it, the copy in the bright corner and a magenta or vermilion price plate as the only other colour.
looks.groundSpec: PALE BRANCH, DELIBERATELY. ca07 c1 #b9f7f6 and cd06 c1 #80dafd both clear 0.55, so the room is repainted: c1, then ink at 0.20, then a vertical gradient of accent 0.18 to ink 0.10, then a white sheen 0.12 to zero, then the hero, then the blind at 0.58/0.29, then a scrim of ink at 0.30. Both inks pass the cool test with room to spare — ca07 #173f3f is R-B = -40, cd06 #1b3d49 is -46 — so the finished ground is a deep teal or deep petrol room, never taupe. The accent does the window light: ca07's #d8360a lays a vermilion wash across the top 40%, cd06's #ab117d a magenta one. The engine's `cast` ground is the whole identity: the product is painted into the background itself (retheme_lab.mjs line 3374 strips every Hero/Lineup product layer once __castBg is set), scaled to min(0.62W/w, 0.92H/h), centred at 0.66W/0.52H, rotated -0.12 rad, alpha 0.92, with a real contact shadow (blur 40, offset 24/30, black at 0.35); then two blurred parallelograms fall across it — blur 26 at full strength with its top edge at 0.62W and its bottom edge at 0.22W, and a blur-60 penumbra at half — so the light rakes from upper-left to lower-right and the copy always lives in the lit upper-left quadrant while the object fills the shadowed right two-thirds. Panels go solid over a cast ground, so every card in the family is the same two things: one lit object, one solid card of facts. You can tell this collection from the other nine at a glance because nothing is tiled, nothing is repeated, nothing overlaps, and there is exactly one product per card at three-quarter scale.

THE PALE-GREY PROBLEM, SOLVED BY A RULE, NOT BY HOPE. On a pale palette (relative luminance of c1 > 0.55) the cast branch repaints the room: c1, then th.ink at 0.20, then a vertical gradient of th.accent 0.18 to th.ink 0.10, then a scrim of th.ink at 0.30. Roughly half the finished ground is the INK colour. So on cast you choose a pale palette by its ink, never by its ground — and the ink must be cool. Programmable form: reject any pale palette whose ink red channel is not at least 16 below its blue channel. That single test passes pa05 (#1b4037), ca07 (#173f3f), ca01 (#183f3c), cd06 (#1b3d49), cd04 (#263f2b) and rejects every warm-inked pale palette — pp02 (#4a3220, +42), pp01, su01-su10, io04, gl02, ck02 — which are exactly the ones that turn taupe and land on the owner's banned "dark orange or brown". pp04 fails at +9, which is why the 62%-scoring Mint Counter Paper is NOT in this collection despite its score. Seven of the ten sit on deep palettes where the branch never veils at all (ground stays c1, sheen 0.10, scrim 0.22 of c1) and the room keeps full chroma; two and a half are the daylight members, drawn only from the cool-inked pale winners.

WHAT THE AUDIT THREW OUT, WITH REASONS I VERIFIED BY OPENING THE FILES. A cast hero is drawn 670px wide, so every fault is at maximum size. poke-slabs-trio is three EMPTY slabs with blank pastel faces and blank label strips — it is the only approved poke- cutout, so this collection has NO Pokémon theme and says so rather than shipping a giant blank. sports-slabs-stack and sports-slabs-fan-five are four and five blank slabs; only sports-slab has a real card face. silver-bars-stack shows silver-coloured bars stamped GOLD; silver-bars-row is stamped "WILD BOLD / 69906"; silver-rounds-pile carries Bitcoin symbols and "UNITED SATES OF AMERICA" — so the silver theme is sterling and silverware, not bullion. coin-graded-fan-three reads "V LODS OF EY / INO COH WO ROUT". strip-boxes-fan is a lateral-flow C/T/S cassette, the same not-diabetes fault the owner rejected strip-vials-pile for; strip-boxes-pile-large is plain kraft cartons. own-stock-macbook-open is a Touch Bar keyboard shot — a relic body and no screen. Every own-apple-* file is the same Cosmic Orange 17 Pro set regardless of "deep-blue" or "silver" in its name, so that theme owns the orange instead of pretending to a colour range. And the qs-* press renders are 400-500px two-up composites: fine small, unusable at 670px. None of these are in any mustShow; all are in the neverShow lists.

looks.name: Clinic Window
looks.oneLine: A glucose meter open in its case, lit from a high window in a sea-green or forest room, with the sealed-and-in-date rule set plainly in the light beside it.
looks.groundSpec: PALE BRANCH, AND THE CLEAREST CASE FOR THE COOL-INK RULE. pa05 c1 #c6faeb and cd04 c1 #91e2a2 both clear 0.55, so the room is repainted: c1, ink at 0.20, a vertical gradient of accent 0.18 to ink 0.10, white sheen 0.12, hero, blind at 0.58 with its 0.29 penumbra, scrim of ink at 0.30. pa05's ink #1b4037 is R-B = -28 and cd04's #263f2b is -5, both cool, so the finished rooms are a deep sea green and a deep forest — clinical, calm, and emphatically not taupe. The window light is the accent: pa05's #c44fbd lays an orchid wash across the top of the room and cd04's #3749e4 a cobalt one, which is what keeps a grey-and-white plastic meter from disappearing into a grey card. This is the only place in the collection where a pale palette is chosen for its subject rather than despite it: a diabetic-supply ad should feel like daylight through a clinic blind, and pa05 is the highest-scoring palette in the whole library at 62%.
looks.imagery: The cast hero is assets/cutouts/strip-kit-meter.webp (1348x1078) and nothing else — a real glucose meter with a test strip in the port, sitting in its open zip case. It is the only honest large image the strips shelf has. strip-boxes-fan is barred outright: I opened it and it is a lateral-flow C/T/S cassette with a red line, which is a rapid test, not a diabetic supply — the same fault the owner rejected strip-boxes-cash and strip-vials-pile for. strip-boxes-pile-large is barred because it is twenty plain kraft cartons that say nothing about what is inside them, which is the owner's blank-unbranded rejection exactly.
neverShow: any pale palette whose ink is warm (pp02, pp04, io04, ck02, gl02, every su id)
a needle, a lancet drawing blood, or any clinical-gore imagery
a CGM brand wordmark over a meter that is not that brand
a second box or kit anywhere on the card
looks.copy: Discreet, procedural, no exclamation — this seller wants to know the rules before they drive over. Headline: CASH FOR TEST STRIPS. Selling point: SEALED, IN-DATE BOXES ONLY. Second selling point: LOCAL PICKUP OR PREPAID MAIL-IN. Items line: OneTouch • FreeStyle • Contour • Accu-Chek • Dexcom Sensors (named in text only, never as a wordmark, because the meter in the picture is not theirs). Price plate: TOP BOX PRICES PAID. CTA: GET YOUR OFFER. Sticker: PAID TODAY.
variations: Sea-green room (pa05) — orchid window light, stepsFlow with three numbered steps
Forest room (cd04) — cobalt window light, checklistHero with the four acceptance rules
Meters cut — headline CASH FOR GLUCOSE METERS, items meters • lancing devices • kits • unopened
Mail-in cut — headline CASH FOR TEST STRIPS with LOCAL PICKUP OR PREPAID MAIL-IN promoted to the money line

looks.name: Slab Under Glass
looks.oneLine: One graded slab lying across a deep violet room like a specimen on a lightbox, the blind cutting over the case, WE BUY SPORTS CARDS in tall condensed caps in the lit corner.
looks.groundSpec: DEEP BRANCH. jw02 c1 #3e3577 (luminance 0.049) is a deep violet; nn02 c1 #241f3b (0.017) a near-black violet. Flat c1, white sheen 0.10, hero, contact shadow black 0.35 blur 40 offset 24/30, blind at 0.50 with the 0.25 penumbra, scrim c1 at 0.22. The hero is wide and short, so min(0.62W/w, 0.92H/h) resolves on the width and the slab lands as a horizontal bar across the middle-right — the blind crosses it at an angle and the acrylic case picks up the seam, which is the single best thing this ground does. Two useful consequences of the deep room: the slab's white card face becomes the brightest value on the card, and the mild upscale on a 523px source is hidden under the blur-26 shadow pass. jw02's accent #fec674 and nn02's #feb263 are the only warm notes and they sit on the price plate.
looks.imagery: The cast hero is assets/cutouts/sports-slab.webp (523x215) and nothing else — the one card asset in the library with a real face in it, a basketball card in a PSA-style case with a red label. Every other card cutout is empty: I opened sports-slabs-stack (four blank slabs), sports-slabs-fan-five and poke-slabs-trio (three empty cases with blank pastel faces and blank label strips). At 670px a blank slab is a 670px blank, which is why they are barred and why this collection has no Pokémon theme at all rather than a Pokémon card with nothing on it.
neverShow: a named athlete in the headline (the card in the picture is a different player)
a Pokémon headline on this theme in any form
a second slab anywhere on the card
looks.copy: Collector-fluent — the words prove you know the market because the picture can only show one card. Headline: WE BUY SPORTS CARDS. Selling point: PSA, BGS AND SGC SLABS OR RAW. Second selling point: WE BUY ENTIRE COLLECTIONS OUTRIGHT. Items line: Rookies • Autos • Patches • Numbered /99. Price plate: UP TO $5,000 PER CARD. CTA: REQUEST AN APPRAISAL. Sticker: PAID TODAY.
variations: Deep violet (jw02) — amber price plate, reviewProof with five stars
Near-black violet (nn02) — the slab as the only lit object, neonNight-adjacent bandKnockout
Grails cut — kicker GRAILS WANTED above the headline, price plate leading with $5,000
Challenge cut — kicker GOT A CARD SHOP QUOTE?, money line WE TOP THE CARD SHOP

looks.name: Forecourt Light
looks.oneLine: One vehicle — a silver sedan, a white pickup or a cargo van — parked large in a cornflower or daylight-teal room with the blind across the flank and a stencilled headline in the light.
looks.groundSpec: ONE DEEP, ONE PALE. du08 c1 #5593ef (luminance 0.290) takes the unveiled path: flat cornflower, white sheen 0.10, hero, black 0.35 contact shadow, blind at 0.50 plus the 0.25 penumbra, scrim c1 at 0.22 — a bright blue forecourt at midday. ca01 c1 #baf8f1 clears 0.55 and takes the pale path, so the room is repainted by its ink #183f3c (R-B = -40, comfortably cool) at 0.20 plus a 0.30 scrim, with its accent #d9322b laying a crimson wash across the top at 0.18 — a deep teal shed with late sun coming through. Both bodies in the pool are white or silver, which is why the room must carry the colour: a white van on a white ground is the grey card, and a white van on a teal ground is a photograph. The blind is at its most literal here, reading as light through a roller door across the vehicle's flank. Big Shoulders Stencil Display is the collection's one stencil face and it belongs on this theme — stencil scored highest of any style at 60% and it reads as fleet marking rather than decoration.
looks.imagery: The cast hero is one of five, matched to the deck the card is running: assets/cutouts/car-sedan-front.webp (2048x1366, a silver sedan in three-quarter front), car-suv-side.webp (1517x618), car-sedan-rear.webp (1937x840), car-truck-front.webp (1869x1599, a white crew-cab pickup) and car-van-cargo.webp (1903x1689, a white high-roof cargo van). All four vehicles are unbadged or ambiguously badged — I checked each one — so the card never claims a make. Keys, titles, wheels and engine bays are barred: this collection's premise is the vehicle itself in the light, and a key fob drawn at three-quarter scale is not the thing the headline names.
neverShow: a truck headline over the sedan hero or the reverse
a second vehicle anywhere on the card
looks.copy: Flat and operational — a tow, a title, a number, no adjectives. Headline: WE BUY CARS (or WE BUY TRUCKS / WE BUY WORK VANS, matched to the vehicle in the ground). Selling point: CASH IN HAND BEFORE WE TOW. Second selling point: TITLE, DMV AND LIEN PAYOFF HANDLED. Items line: Title In Hand • Running Or Not • High Miles • Salvage • Free Tow. Price plate: UP TO $15,000 CASH (trucks $25,000, vans $20,000). CTA: GET AN INSTANT OFFER. Sticker: SAME DAY. Comparative cut allowed on named wholesale buyers only, without an apostrophe-S: WE MATCH CARVANA, WE TOP CARMAX.
variations: Cornflower forecourt (du08) with the silver sedan — headline WE BUY CARS
Daylight teal (ca01) with the white pickup — crimson window light, headline WE BUY TRUCKS
Van cut — car-van-cargo as the hero, headline WE BUY WORK VANS, items Transit • Sprinter • ProMaster • Fleet Lots, kicker FLEETS OK
Challenge cut — WE MATCH CARVANA with the promise line Their offer, minus the ladders: same number, paid before we leave.

looks.name: Garage Night
looks.oneLine: A naked motorcycle standing large in a midnight-navy or oxblood garage with a hard blind across the tank and tyre, and the title-or-not promise glowing in the corner.
looks.groundSpec: DEEP BRANCH, THE NIGHT END OF THE FAMILY. nn01 c1 #0e253c (luminance 0.017) is a midnight navy; nn04 c1 #39181e (0.016) an oxblood so dark it reads as near-black with a red cast rather than as brown — worth stating because the owner bans anything landing as dark orange or brown, and the guard is that at luminance 0.016 no hue reads as a brown, only as a temperature. Flat c1, white sheen 0.10, hero at 0.66W/0.52H at -0.12 rad, contact shadow black 0.35 blur 40 offset 24/30, blind at 0.50 with the blur-60 penumbra at 0.25, scrim c1 at 0.22. The bike is mostly black — engine, frame, tyres — with a white tank, so the room must be darker than the bike's darks or the silhouette flattens; nn01 and nn04 both are. nn01's accent #fcaca5 and nn04's #32ea50 are the neon: one blush, one acid green, on the price plate and the sticker, which is what makes neonNight the natural first layout here. IF nn04 EVER READS BROWN ON A PROOF, fall back to nn01 and do not substitute a lighter warm palette.
looks.imagery: The cast hero is assets/cutouts/car-motorcycle-side.webp (1790x1886) and nothing else — a modern naked bike from the rear three-quarter, white tank, black engine, chain and rear tyre in full. It carries no readable badge, which is precisely why this theme never wears a marque: the shop buys Harleys and Yamahas and says so in the items line, but the machine in the picture is not one of them and the card must not imply it is.
neverShow: a helmet, a rider or a road scene
a second machine anywhere on the card
looks.copy: Short and unsentimental, the way a bike gets sold at nine at night. Headline: WE BUY MOTORCYCLES. Selling point: TITLE OR NOT, RUNNING OR NOT. Second selling point: CASH IN HAND BEFORE WE LOAD IT. Items line: Harley • Honda • Yamaha • Kawasaki • Dirt Bikes • Scooters (named in text only — no wordmark, because the bike in the picture is unbadged). Price plate: UP TO $12,000 CASH. CTA: GET AN INSTANT OFFER. Sticker: CASH TODAY.
variations: Midnight navy (nn01) — blush neon on the price plate, neonNight
Oxblood (nn04) — acid-green neon, the tyre edge catching the blind
Pickup cut — FREE PICKUP ACROSS LA & OC promoted to the money line, trustSeal
Proof cut — reviewProof with five stars and the two promise lines, the bike untouched behind them

A cast hero is drawn 670px wide, so every fault is at maximum size. poke-slabs-trio is three EMPTY slabs with blank pastel faces and blank label strips — it is the only approved poke- cutout, so this collection has NO Pokémon theme and says so rather than shipping a giant blank. sports-slabs-stack and sports-slabs-fan-five are four and five blank slabs; only sports-slab has a real card face. silver-bars-stack shows silver-coloured bars stamped GOLD; silver-bars-row is stamped "WILD BOLD / 69906"; silver-rounds-pile carries Bitcoin symbols and "UNITED SATES OF AMERICA" — so the silver theme is sterling and silverware, not bullion. coin-graded-fan-three reads "V LODS OF EY / INO COH WO ROUT". strip-boxes-fan is a lateral-flow C/T/S cassette, the same not-diabetes fault the owner rejected strip-vials-pile for; strip-boxes-pile-large is plain kraft cartons. own-stock-macbook-open is a Touch Bar keyboard shot — a relic body and no screen. looks.name: Gem Label
looks.oneLine: The real graded-slab frame fills the card, WE BUY / POKÉMON typed on the paper label like a grade line, a 1999 Charizard washed pale in the window below, and a 10 / GEM MT block at the right.
looks.groundSpec: slabFrame() paints the whole ground. sports-slab-graded (1572x1425) scales to H=1080, so dw=1191 and ox=-56 — the frame bleeds off both edges by 56px, which is correct, not a crop error. Frame shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.35), blur 50, offsetY 18. LABEL box y 59 to 286 (h 227), painted rgba(c1,0.06) so ck02's #fbf5f5 stays paper-white; the headline is forced to #17171a (theme ink is used only when its luminance is under 0.35), stripped of gradient, shadow and stroke, and scaled into the left 66% at k<=1.8 — the engine already enforces one sentence, one face, one colour there, which is why a typewriter face survives it. Divider: 2px rgba(20,20,24,0.55) at 68% of the label. Barcode: bars 2-5px wide, height 0.12 of the label, #1a1a1e, running 72% to 96%. WINDOW box y 335 to 1026 (1027x691, a 1.49:1 letterbox — wider than a real card, which is why copy and not a portrait card belongs in it). Window fill rgba(c1,0.97), then the photograph cover-fit at k=max(w/iw,h/ih)*1.02, then rgba(c1,0.66) over it, then a corner gradient from rgba(c2,0.35) to transparent. Both palettes here are pale, so that 0.66 wash is a warm white veil and the Charizard reads as a tinted ghost, not a picture competing with the type. PALE/DEEP SPLIT: on a deep palette the same 0.66 wash turns the window near-black and the photo disappears — that is why this theme is locked to pale grounds and Case Light takes the deep ones. bg.scrim stays 0.001 (the ground is already painted) and __dg=true, so the canvas keeps its own colour instead of being greyscaled.
looks.imagery: assets/cutouts/sports-slab-graded.webp as the frame — the blank front-on graded holder, label bar over a landscape window. In the window: assets/bg-web/pokemon-charizard-card-1.jpg (1920x1280, lum 0.353, detail 9.21), which really shows a PSA-slabbed 1999 Pokémon Game Charizard Holo GEM MT 10 standing on an easel — so the copy's PSA 10 and Charizard are literally in the frame. WATERMARK CONTROL: the photographer's script mark sits bottom-right; the window's bottom-right 26% x 18% must carry a solid spec chip in the accent reading 1999 BASE SET · PSA 10, which covers it. No cutout layer is added — the frame and the window are the whole image.

looks.name: Five Star Slab
looks.oneLine: The same graded frame turned to sports: WE BUY / SPORTS CARDS stencilled on the label, four red-labelled slabs fitted whole into the window, and five stars over TOP RATED where the grade number would be.
looks.groundSpec: Same frame geometry as Gem Label (dw 1191, ox -56, label y 59-286, window y 335-1026). The difference is what fills the window and how. WEBBG.sports is EMPTY — there is not one approved sports photograph in assets/bg-web — so slabFrame() falls to the cutout branch, sets __cut=true, and FITS rather than covers: k=min((1027-60)/iw,(691-60)/ih), then a lighter rgba(c1,0.55) wash instead of 0.66. sports-slabs-stack at 1843x1328 gives k=0.475 → 875x631 sitting whole inside the window with air around it, crisp, no crop. Both palettes are pale (ca07 #b9f7f6, ca05 #d4eeff), so the wash is a pale aqua veil and the slabs' red label bars stay legible through it — that red is the only warm note on a cool card and it must survive; if it does not, drop the wash to 0.48 rather than lightening the palette. Grade block: run LAB_SLABGRADE=stars so the right of the label carries ★★★★★ at fontSize 0.22 of the label height with charSpacing 60, over TOP RATED at 0.10 with charSpacing 180. On ca07 the accent #d8360a clears the 0.62 luminance test so the stars take the accent; on ca05 #a16f12 also clears it and the stars go gold.
looks.imagery: assets/cutouts/sports-slab-graded.webp as the frame. In the window: assets/cutouts/sports-slabs-stack.webp — four portrait graded slabs fanned left to right, each with a red label bar across the top and a blank cream card below. looks.copy: Clipped and plain — stencil says it once and stops. Headline: WE BUY / SPORTS CARDS. Selling point: PSA, BGS AND SGC SLABS OR RAW. Second: WE BUY ENTIRE COLLECTIONS OUTRIGHT. looks.name: Case Light
looks.oneLine: The graded frame floating on a deep jewel-blue field like a slab under a display-case lamp, with a serif headline on the paper label and the window kept dark and quiet.
looks.groundSpec: Same frame and boxes, deep ground. jw01 #1f3e7a and jw09 #054666 are both under 0.22 luminance, so this is the DEEP branch of the slab paint: the c1 fill plus the c2-to-transparent diagonal gradient reads as a dark blue field, and the frame's rgba(0,0,0,0.35) blur-50 shadow lifts the acrylic off it — that is the display-case effect. Two consequences to honour. (1) The label is painted rgba(c1,0.06) — a 6% whisper of deep blue over paper-white — so the label stays the one bright object on a dark card and the serif headline lands as #17171a on white; that contrast jump IS the theme. (2) The window's rgba(c1,0.55) wash is now a dark blue veil, so the fitted slab sits low-key and the copy over it is the loudest thing; do not raise the wash further or the window goes solid. Grade block: 10 / GEM MT — and because the theme ink here is #d7deec / #d2e0ea (luminance well over 0.35) the engine falls back to #17171a for the label type, which is correct and keeps the label reading as paper. Trust marks must take real fills on this ground, never translucent plates.
looks.imagery: assets/cutouts/sports-slab-graded.webp as the frame; assets/cutouts/sports-slabs-stack.webp fitted into the window at k=0.475 under the deep wash. The red label bars go plum under a blue veil — accepted here, because this theme is about the case, not the label.

looks.name: Cert Cast
looks.oneLine: One slab drawn large into a near-white ground under a soft diagonal window shadow, with the phone number and the money line set in mono like a certification number.
looks.groundSpec: The cast ground, pale branch, since ck09 #f3f8fa and pp07 #eff7fe both clear 0.55. Sequence: fill c1; lay rgba(ink,0.20) over the whole card so a near-white ground does not read as the blank 'what is this light theme' card; then a vertical gradient from rgba(accent,0.18) to rgba(ink,0.10); then a white sheen from 0.12 to transparent across the top-left 55%. The product is placed at 0.66W, 0.52H, rotated -0.12rad, scaled k=min(670/iw, 993/ih), alpha 0.92, with a rgba(0,0,0,0.35) blur-40 shadow offset 24/30. Over that the window shadow: a blur-26 rgba(8,10,16,0.58) wedge running from 0.62W at the top to 0.22W at the bottom, plus a blur-60 penumbra at half strength. Final scrim rgba(c2 or ink, 0.30). Because both accents are blue (#0c658d, #0378c7) the card reads as a blueprint or a cert document, which is the point. All panels over this ground go solid at rgba(deep,0.9) automatically — do not fight that, it is what keeps the small mono type legible.
looks.imagery: Pokémon cards cast assets/cutouts/poke-slabs-trio.webp (1794x1831 — three acrylic cases lying flat and fanned, blank white labels, pastel peach/mint/pink inserts; k=0.373, so 670x684 from a 1794px source, crisp). Sports cards cast assets/cutouts/sports-slabs-stack.webp (1843x1328, k=0.364 → 670x483, crisp). Nothing else is placed — the cast product IS the imagery.

looks.copy: Technical and exact, the voice of a written offer. Headline: WE BUY / SPORTS CARDS or WE BUY / POKÉMON in Audiowide, two words a line, never more. Selling point: PSA, BGS AND SGC SLABS OR RAW (sports) or GRADED SLABS AND RAW, PSA 10 TO UNGRADED (Pokémon). Second: FREE APPRAISAL, WE SORT IT FOR YOU. The mono numerals carry the money line (UP TO $5,000 PER CARD / UP TO $10,000 PER CARD) and (562) 999-4994, and those are the only numbers on the card — no invented cert or pop figures, because we cannot back them.
variations: Blueprint (ck09) — Chalk, #0c658d on #f3f8fa with the near-black support; the cleanest.
Document (pp07) — Paper, #0378c7 with the #c0765f terracotta kept to the rules only; warmer, better on the sports side.
Shadow long — push the window-shadow wedge origin from 0.62W to 0.70W so the light comes in flatter and the slab sits in more of it.

looks.name: Grade Wall
looks.oneLine: A four-by-three lattice of the same graded slab under a deep navy veil, with a short pixel headline knocked out over it — the showcase wall, honest about being one slab repeated.
looks.groundSpec: The tile ground: 4 columns, 3 rows, gap 28, so each cell is 235 x 322.7. Each cell holds the object at k=min((235-24)/iw,(322.7-24)/ih)*0.96 with a rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur-26 shadow offset 10/16 — real drop shadows, even gaps, no overlap. Field colour is c1 when its luminance clears 0.55: lp08 #eef4fe and cd07 #b1cefc both do. The veil is the theme ink (lp08 #2b384f, cd07 #2a384f, both under 0.4 luminance) at scrim 0.6, so the finished card is a deep navy field with a pale blue lattice glowing through it — that is the look, and it is why both palettes here are blue. THE HONEST PART: the pool is built from the deck's own cuts prefixes and gated at pool.length >= 4. The Pokémon deck yields exactly one approved cutout, so today this card takes the engine's existing next step in ['tile','cast'] and renders as its cast sibling — a graceful, already-coded fallback, not a broken card. The wall as specified needs that gate to accept a card pool of one to three; when it does, the lattice is twelve copies of one slab, which is what a showcase actually looks like and is not a repeat in the sense the standing rules forbid (that rule is about lines of copy). Panels over this ground go solid at rgba(deep,0.9) automatically — required, or the small type dies on the lattice.
looks.imagery: Twelve cells of assets/cutouts/poke-slabs-trio.webp — three flat acrylic cases with blank labels and pastel inserts, at 211px wide per cell where the asset is 1794px native, so downscaled and sharp. The pastel peach/mint/pink inserts are the reason both palettes are cool blue: the cells supply the warmth, the field supplies the cold.

I audited the card pool before designing anything and it is smaller than the brief assumes. `assets/approved-assets.json` approves exactly THREE card cutouts: poke-slabs-trio, sports-slab, sports-slabs-stack. poke-cards-fan — named in my brief — is REJECTED as "blank-unbranded", as are poke-slab, poke-binder-open, poke-booster*, poke-elite-box, poke-packs-pile, sports-cards*, sports-binder-open, sports-box-sealed, sports-slabs-fan-five. Naming any of them is a hard fail. sports-slab-graded and poke-graded-slab are rejected as products but kept as the SLAB FRAME (slabFrame() in retheme_lab.mjs hard-codes sports-slab-graded and returns early unless cat is pokemon or sports — the owner's card-only rule, verified in code, so no coin ever enters a slab here). In assets/bg-web there are ZERO approved sports photographs (all five sit in bg-web-rejected) and exactly TWO pokemon ones, both takes of the same PSA GEM MT 10 Charizard on a table at NYCC 2021, CC BY-SA 2.0, with the photographer's script watermark in the bottom-right corner. I opened all of them: poke-slabs-trio is three acrylic cases lying flat with BLANK white labels and pastel peach/mint/pink inserts — no Pokémon anywhere in the frame; sports-slabs-stack is four portrait slabs fanned with a RED PSA-style label bar, the best card asset in the repo; sports-slab is 523x215px, a real basketball card in a slab at a steep angle — the only asset showing a card face, and far too small to enlarge.

WHAT THAT FORCES. A 12-cell wall of DIFFERENT card objects does not exist and cannot be faked. So the wall here is a lattice of the same graded slab repeated, the way a shop showcase actually looks — designed for, not apologised for. I verified the gate: the tile ground pools only cutouts matching the deck's own `cuts` prefixes and requires pool.length >= 4; the card decks yield 1-2, so both tile themes fall through the engine's existing ['tile','cast'] chain to their cast sibling until that gate learns about card decks. Both tile specs name the cast fallback as a designed state, not an accident.

WHAT HOLDS THE TEN TOGETHER. Every card in this collection is presented as a GRADED ITEM. A label strip runs across the top carrying the headline like a grade line, with a hairline divider at 68% and a barcode from 72% to 96%; a grade block sits at 84% — either 10 / GEM MT or five stars / TOP RATED, never four, never six. Below it is a window holding the thing being bought. Three themes use the real slab frame for that shape; the other seven draw it. Second signature: every numeral on every card is monospace, JetBrains Mono or DM Mono, because cards are a numbers hobby — cert numbers, pop counts, /99 print runs. Third: every support face is a plain grotesque (Satoshi, Manrope, Chivo, Sora, Libre Franklin, Instrument Sans), so ten different display faces never make ten different cards. Fourth: the only competitors named are card companies — TCGPLAYER, GAMESTOP, THE CARD SHOP for Pokémon; GOLDIN, FANATICS, THE CARD SHOP for sports — and never with an apostrophe-S.

THE MARK LAW, the sharpest thing I found. ELEMENTS.pokemon hard-codes its decorative marks to #ffcb05 / #2a75bb / #cc0000 with emoji, whatever palette the card wears — so a mint or orchid palette on a Pokémon card gets red, blue and yellow confetti it did not ask for, which IS the "jumbled colour mess". The one documented escape is ELEMENTS_FAMILY['Lined Paper'], which swaps them for the theme's own accent and ink and sets noEmoji. Therefore: every Pokémon theme here either wears a red- or blue-accented palette, so the locked marks read as Pokémon brand colour on purpose, or wears an lp* palette, so the marks take the theme's colour. Every palette in this set was chosen against that test.

Grounds are deliberately narrow — slab 3, cast 4, tile 2, paper 1 — with no Apple scene (those photographs are iPhones and MacBooks, never a card) and no web photo as a card's ground (28% measured, and the only card photo is licence-encumbered and watermarked; it appears only inside a slab window, at one-third size, with a spec chip over the corner where the watermark lands).

AT A GLANCE. Every other collection shows you a product. This one shows you a slab: a label band, a barcode, a grade, and a window. If a card in this set has no label strip and no grade block, it is not from this collection.

looks.name: Rookie Board
looks.oneLine: The same lattice turned to sports — red-labelled slabs in even rows behind a navy veil, condensed type stacked like a scoreboard, and a gold five-star row for the grade.
looks.groundSpec: Identical lattice mechanics: 4 x 3, gap 28, cells 235 x 322.7, per-cell fit k=min((cw-24)/iw,(chh-24)/ih)*0.96, shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur 26 offset 10/16. Field: ck05 #f5f7fb and ca09 #c8f2fe both clear 0.55. Veil: ck05 ink #2c3850 and ca09 ink #193e47 are both under 0.4, so scrim 0.6 again — the collection's two tile themes land on the same 60% deep veil, which is what makes them read as siblings rather than as two ideas. THIS IS THE ONE PLACE sports-slab BELONGS. At 523x215 it cannot be enlarged, but a cell only asks for 211px wide, so it renders at native scale and stays crisp — and it is the only approved asset in the repo that shows an actual card face, a real basketball card in a slab with its red label and barcode. Mixing it with sports-slabs-stack gives a pool of two: alternating the flat-angle and the fanned-portrait cells gives the wall a rhythm instead of a stamp. Same gate caveat as Grade Wall — the pool is two and the gate wants four, so today this falls through to cast on sports-slabs-stack, which is specified, not accidental.
looks.imagery: Cells alternate assets/cutouts/sports-slab.webp (523x215, one graded slab at a steep low angle holding a real basketball card, red PSA-style label and barcode visible) and assets/cutouts/sports-slabs-stack.webp (1843x1328, four fanned portrait slabs with red label bars). The red label bar is the only warm colour on the card and the veil must not swallow it — if it does, drop the scrim to 0.54 rather than lightening the field.
mustShow: red label bars legible through the veil
looks.copy: Scoreboard cadence — short stacked lines, numbers doing the talking. Headline: WE BUY / SPORTS CARDS in Teko. Selling point: ROOKIE AUTOS, PATCHES AND NUMBERED. Second: PSA, BGS AND SGC SLABS OR RAW. Items line Grails Wanted • Rookies • Autos • Patches • Numbered /99 • Wemby • Ohtani • Clark. Money line UP TO $5,000 PER CARD, CTA REQUEST AN APPRAISAL, sticker PAID TODAY. Marks are the category's own — cardSlab, star5, medal — never a theme ornament.
variations: Night board (ck05) — Chalk, electric #123cef on a navy veil; the sharpest.
Trophy board (ca09) — Cool Air, gold #b36314 accent with teal support; warmer, and it suits the five-star row.
Alternating rows — sports-slab on rows one and three, sports-slabs-stack on row two, so the wall has a horizon instead of a texture.
