looks.name: Want List
looks.oneLine: The buyer's want list written on ruled paper in pen, the items line broken into a real checklist, and one slab taped into the margin as a specimen.
looks.groundSpec: The drawn paper grounds, not a photograph. paper:ruled is #fbf7ea stock with 2.2px #9fb9df rules every 54px starting at y=150, a 2.2px #e08f8f margin rule at x=118, three punched holes at 18%, 50% and 82% height, 9000 specks of fibre noise at up to 3.5% black, and a binding shadow from rgba(0,0,0,0.10) to transparent across the top 70px. paper:grid (#f7f9fb, 1.4px #b9cbe2 at 48px) is the alternate. These are cached like any backdrop and keepColour is true for paper:, so the sheet is never greyscaled or tinted — it stays paper. The palette does not paint the ground here; it paints the PEN. Both palettes are Lined Paper family, which is the whole reason for this theme: ELEMENTS_FAMILY['Lined Paper'] replaces the locked Pokémon #ffcb05/#2a75bb/#cc0000 marks with [accent, ink, accent] and sets noEmoji, so a Pokémon card on this ground gets hand-drawn marks in #084f88 or #920c03 and no emoji at all. That is the only documented way to run a Pokémon card without brand-colour confetti, and it makes this the one theme in the set equally safe on both categories. Highlighter bands and sticky-note plates come with the family; keep them to the money line and one badge. PALE ONLY — a deep palette has no meaning on a drawn sheet.
looks.imagery: One slab, small, in the right margin at roughly 260px wide with a slight tilt and a tape strip across one corner: assets/cutouts/poke-slabs-trio.webp on the Pokémon run, assets/cutouts/sports-slabs-stack.webp on the sports run. It is a specimen pinned to the list, not a hero — the list is the picture. Never both on one card.
mustShow: checklist built from the items line
neverShow: non-Lined-Paper palette (brings back the locked marks and emoji)
poke-slabs-trio and sports-slabs-stack on the same card
looks.copy: Written, not proclaimed — the voice of someone who keeps a list. Headline: WE BUY / POKÉMON or WE BUY / SPORTS CARDS in Zilla Slab, sitting on a rule as if it were written on the line. Selling point: GRADED SLABS AND RAW, PSA 10 TO UNGRADED (Pokémon) or ROOKIE AUTOS, PATCHES AND NUMBERED (sports). The items line becomes the list itself, one entry per rule with a pen tick: Charizard, Moonbreon, alt arts, illustration rares — or rookies, autos, patches, numbered /99. Money line UP TO $10,000 PER CARD or UP TO $5,000 PER CARD, CTA REQUEST AN APPRAISAL, sticker FREE QUOTE.
variations: Blue pen (lp01) — #084f88 ink with the #9d8518 gold on the ticks; the default.
Red pen (lp07) — #920c03 with #1091c8 blue for the rules; reads as a corrected list, sharper.
Graph paper — swap paper:ruled for paper:grid and set the list in two columns; better when the items line runs long.

looks.name: Shop Callout
looks.oneLine: A knockout band across a cast slab that names the buyer you already tried — WE MATCH / THE CARD SHOP — with the TCGplayer or GameStop wordmark parked in a clear corner.
looks.groundSpec: Cast ground, and this is the theme where the pale/deep split actually changes the build. ik02 #e8f1fa is over 0.55, so it takes the PALE branch: c1, then rgba(ink,0.20) over the whole card, then the accent-to-ink gradient (0.18 to 0.10), window shadow at strength 0.58, final scrim rgba(c2 or ink, 0.30). du08 #5593ef sits near 0.30, so it takes the DEEP branch: no ink overlay, no accent gradient, window shadow at 0.50, final scrim rgba(c1, 0.22) — a lighter veil on a stronger ground. The band is the loudest object either way: a knockout bar sized to the word, taking the accent (#bf3a00 or #3c3e65), with the competitor name reversed out of it — never a full-bleed band, which turns into a slab. The wordmark goes in the best clear corner at 230, 190 or 150px wide with a 10px keep-out, re-inked white on the deep palette and to ink on the pale one; that is the engine's own logo placement and it only fires on words it already maps, so until the card brands join that map the theme runs on the word alone and stays correct.
looks.imagery: One cast slab: assets/cutouts/sports-slabs-stack.webp for sports, assets/cutouts/poke-slabs-trio.webp for Pokémon, at 0.66W / 0.52H rotated -0.12rad under the diagonal window shadow. Plus exactly one wordmark from assets/logos — tcgplayer.png or gamestop.png on a Pokémon card, fanatics-inc.png on a sports card. One mark per card, never two, never a grading company: there is no psa, beckett, cgc, sgc or goldin file in assets/logos and inventing one is a hard fail.
mustShow: competitor name drawn from CHALLENGE (TCGPLAYER, GAMESTOP, THE CARD SHOP, FANATICS)
knockout band sized to the word
neverShow: two brand marks on one card
unbounded claims (any offer, beat anyone, best price)
tcgplayer or gamestop on a SPORTS CARDS headline
looks.copy: Comparative and specific, never a superlative — we name who, and we say what we do differently. Kicker: LOWBALLED BY TCGPLAYER? Headline: WE MATCH / THE CARD SHOP — no apostrophe-S, ever. Selling point: 'We match the TCGPLAYER number without the hoops: no fees, no waiting, cash today.' Money line: BRING YOUR TCGPLAYER QUOTE — WE TOP IT. CTA REQUEST AN APPRAISAL, sticker ON THE SPOT. The company named in the kicker, the money line and the promise must be the same one, and it must match the mark in the corner.
variations: Ink Pop (ik02) — pale ground with the #bf3a00 band; the cleanest read of the bar.
Duotone (du08) — the mid-blue deep branch, navy band, white-inked wordmark; heavier, and the better fit for bandKnockout.
Name in the band — put the competitor inside the knockout bar with WE MATCH above it rather than the reverse; use when the name runs over twelve characters.

looks.name: Collector Reviews
looks.oneLine: A seller's own words on a quote card, five stars above it, with one slab cast softly behind — the review that says we knew what the card was worth.
looks.groundSpec: Cast ground, pale branch on both palettes (lp03 #eef6ee and lp09 #eaf7f2 clear 0.55 comfortably): c1, rgba(ink,0.20), the accent-to-ink gradient at 0.18/0.10, the slab at 0.66W / 0.52H rotated -0.12rad with its rgba(0,0,0,0.35) blur-40 shadow, the blur-26 window wedge at strength 0.58 plus the blur-60 penumbra, final scrim rgba(c2 or ink, 0.30). Deliberately the softest ground in the set — the quote card is the subject and the slab is the room it sits in, so pull the cast product's alpha from 0.92 down to 0.80 and let it sit behind the quote rather than beside it. The quote card takes a solid fill from the palette, not a translucent plate, which the cast ground enforces anyway. Both palettes are Lined Paper family, so on the Pokémon run the marks become pen-coloured and the emoji are dropped — a review card with lightning bolts and playing-card emoji scattered over it would undo the whole tone, which is exactly why lp was chosen here. Five stars, always five.
looks.imagery: One cast slab behind the quote card: assets/cutouts/poke-slabs-trio.webp on the Pokémon run, assets/cutouts/sports-slabs-stack.webp on the sports run. Nothing sits over the type, and the slab never crosses the quote card — the trust stack yields to the product everywhere else in the library, and here the product yields to the quote.
mustShow: quote drawn from the category's own QUOTES pool with a name and a local city
neverShow: star rows of four or six
invented review text not in the QUOTES pool
review city outside LONG BEACH, LAKEWOOD, DOWNEY, CARSON, TORRANCE, CERRITOS, BELLFLOWER, SIGNAL HILL
sports quote on a POKÉMON headline
pokemon quote on a SPORTS CARDS headline
reviewProof as the only layout in a run (it flips the lab into review-page mode)
looks.copy: First person, past tense, ordinary — the quote does the selling and the headline stays out of its way. Headline: WE BUY / POKÉMON. Quote: 'They knew what the alt arts were worth.' — Marcus T., Long Beach, CA. On the sports run: 'Graded slabs priced against real comps.' — Rosa V., Lakewood, CA. Rating line 4.9★ 200+ LOCAL REVIEWS. Selling point: FREE APPRAISAL, WE SORT IT FOR YOU. CTA REQUEST AN APPRAISAL. Money line stays bounded at UP TO $10,000 PER CARD or UP TO $5,000 PER CARD.
variations: Green tick (lp03) — #055e17 pen, with the five stars and the ticks in the same green; reads as verified.
Teal (lp09) — #0c5b46 with the #f24f6a coral kept to the star row only.
Two quotes — a second, shorter quote under the first on stepsFlow; only where the card has room below the money line.

THE HONEST PREMISE. I audited the card pool before designing anything and it is smaller than the brief assumes. `assets/approved-assets.json` approves exactly THREE card cutouts: poke-slabs-trio, sports-slab, sports-slabs-stack. poke-cards-fan — named in my brief — is REJECTED as "blank-unbranded", as are poke-slab, poke-binder-open, poke-booster*, poke-elite-box, poke-packs-pile, sports-cards*, sports-binder-open, sports-box-sealed, sports-slabs-fan-five. Naming any of them is a hard fail. sports-slab-graded and poke-graded-slab are rejected as products but kept as the SLAB FRAME (slabFrame() in retheme_lab.mjs hard-codes sports-slab-graded and returns early unless cat is pokemon or sports — the owner's card-only rule, verified in code, so no coin ever enters a slab here). In assets/bg-web there are ZERO approved sports photographs (all five sit in bg-web-rejected) and exactly TWO pokemon ones, both takes of the same PSA GEM MT 10 Charizard on a table at NYCC 2021, CC BY-SA 2.0, with the photographer's script watermark in the bottom-right corner. I opened all of them: poke-slabs-trio is three acrylic cases lying flat with BLANK white labels and pastel peach/mint/pink inserts — no Pokémon anywhere in the frame; sports-slabs-stack is four portrait slabs fanned with a RED PSA-style label bar, the best card asset in the repo; sports-slab is 523x215px, a real basketball card in a slab at a steep angle — the only asset showing a card face, and far too small to enlarge.

WHAT THAT FORCES. A 12-cell wall of DIFFERENT card objects does not exist and cannot be faked. So the wall here is a lattice of the same graded slab repeated, the way a shop showcase actually looks — designed for, not apologised for. I verified the gate: the tile ground pools only cutouts matching the deck's own `cuts` prefixes and requires pool.length >= 4; the card decks yield 1-2, so both tile themes fall through the engine's existing ['tile','cast'] chain to their cast sibling until that gate learns about card decks. Both tile specs name the cast fallback as a designed state, not an accident.

WHAT HOLDS THE TEN TOGETHER. Every card in this collection is presented as a GRADED ITEM. A label strip runs across the top carrying the headline like a grade line, with a hairline divider at 68% and a barcode from 72% to 96%; a grade block sits at 84% — either 10 / GEM MT or five stars / TOP RATED, never four, never six. Below it is a window holding the thing being bought. Three themes use the real slab frame for that shape; the other seven draw it. Second signature: every numeral on every card is monospace, JetBrains Mono or DM Mono, because cards are a numbers hobby — cert numbers, pop counts, /99 print runs. Third: every support face is a plain grotesque (Satoshi, Manrope, Chivo, Sora, Libre Franklin, Instrument Sans), so ten different display faces never make ten different cards. Fourth: the only competitors named are card companies — TCGPLAYER, GAMESTOP, THE CARD SHOP for Pokémon; GOLDIN, FANATICS, THE CARD SHOP for sports — and never with an apostrophe-S.

THE MARK LAW, the sharpest thing I found. ELEMENTS.pokemon hard-codes its decorative marks to #ffcb05 / #2a75bb / #cc0000 with emoji, whatever palette the card wears — so a mint or orchid palette on a Pokémon card gets red, blue and yellow confetti it did not ask for, which IS the "jumbled colour mess". The one documented escape is ELEMENTS_FAMILY['Lined Paper'], which swaps them for the theme's own accent and ink and sets noEmoji. Therefore: every Pokémon theme here either wears a red- or blue-accented palette, so the locked marks read as Pokémon brand colour on purpose, or wears an lp* palette, so the marks take the theme's colour. Every palette in this set was chosen against that test.

Grounds are deliberately narrow — slab 3, cast 4, tile 2, paper 1 — with no Apple scene (those photographs are iPhones and MacBooks, never a card) and no web photo as a card's ground (28% measured, and the only card photo is licence-encumbered and watermarked; it appears only inside a slab window, at one-third size, with a spec chip over the corner where the watermark lands).

AT A GLANCE. Every other collection shows you a product. This one shows you a slab: a label band, a barcode, a grade, and a window. If a card in this set has no label strip and no grade block, it is not from this collection.

looks.name: Raw And Graded
looks.oneLine: Three empty acrylic cases cast large on a pale blue field, saying plainly that we buy them graded or loose and sort it out ourselves.
looks.groundSpec: Cast ground, pale branch (pa07 #dcf0ff and io07 #feebe9 both clear 0.55): c1, then rgba(ink,0.20) — #213b4d or #4d2f2c — then the vertical accent-to-ink gradient at 0.18/0.10, then the white sheen across the top-left. Product at 0.66W / 0.52H, k=min(670/1794, 993/1831)=0.373 so 670x684 from a 1794px source, native and crisp, rotated -0.12rad with the rgba(0,0,0,0.35) blur-40 shadow at 24/30. Window wedge at 0.58, penumbra at half. Final scrim rgba(c2 or ink, 0.30). THE PALETTE IS CHOSEN BY THE ASSET: poke-slabs-trio has peach, mint and pink inserts in its windows, and pa07's pale blue field with a #e44920 red-orange accent is the only pastel in the library that holds all three without arguing with them — the card is pastel because the object is pastel. Both accents are red-family, which is the other requirement: this is a non-Lined-Paper palette, so the locked #ffcb05 / #2a75bb / #cc0000 marks stay on, and they only read as intentional next to a red accent. Never run this theme on a mint, teal, orchid or violet palette.
looks.imagery: assets/cutouts/poke-slabs-trio.webp, cast large and alone: three graded holders lying flat and fanned at a low three-quarter angle, blank white labels, pastel inserts where the card face would be. Described honestly — there is no Pokémon in this frame, which is exactly why the copy claims sorting and appraisal rather than naming a grail. If the card needs to name Charizard, it belongs on Gem Label, where a real Charizard is in the window.
neverShow: mint, teal, orchid or violet palette (fights the locked marks)
copy:SEALED BOOSTER BOXES AND VINTAGE WOTC
naming a specific grail over an image of blank slabs
drawn or generated card art in the empty windows
Barlow Condensed on a curved path
looks.copy: Plain and reassuring — the theme for the person with a shoebox, not a grail. Headline: WE BUY / POKÉMON in Barlow Condensed. Selling point: GRADED SLABS AND RAW, PSA 10 TO UNGRADED. Second: FREE APPRAISAL, WE SORT IT FOR YOU. Kicker CARD BUYER rather than GRAILS WANTED, because the image is three empty holders and the claim has to match the picture. Money line UP TO $10,000 PER CARD, CTA REQUEST AN APPRAISAL, sticker SAME DAY.
variations: Pastel blue (pa07) — #dcf0ff field with the #e44920 accent; the intended read, and Pastel is the 62% family.
Warm (io07) — #feebe9 with the true red #e62b34; louder, and the closest of the two to the locked mark colours.
Flat lay — drop the -0.12rad rotation to level and raise the product to 0.50H so the three cases read as a row on a counter rather than a cast object.

looks.name: Gold Bar Wall
looks.oneLine: Twelve gold cutouts lie flat in the 4x3 lattice under a 60% olive-ink wash, CASH FOR GOLD stencilled across the middle band, and PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE set in mono under it.
looks.groundSpec: Parent gold deck (LAB_SUBCATS=0), so the wall pool is the first twelve approved gold- cutouts and the lattice is always full. Lattice: COLS 4, ROWS 3, gap 28, cell 235 x 322, each cutout scaled min((cell-24)/w,(cell-24)/h)*0.96 and centred, drop shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur 26 offset +10/+16 - real shadows, no overlap, no ghosting. PALE PALETTE (pp04 c1 #f2f8ef, pa04 c1 #d9f7d3, both lum>0.55): the wall is painted straight onto c1 and then washed with the INK - pp04 #2e3d25, pa04 #2b3e27 - at 0.60, so the card reads as gold on olive-black and the accent (pp04 leaf green #4a8704, pa04 violet #9265ee) is the only other colour. There is no deep variant of this theme; if a deep palette is ever swapped in, the wall paints on the neutral #eceef2 fallback instead of c1 and the wash becomes c1 at 0.60, which is the Jeweller's Case card, not this one. Every stat tile, review card and step panel goes solid at rgba(ink,0.9) with white copy - that is the engine's own behaviour over a busy ground and it is what keeps the small copy legible against the bars. Density target: the wall shows through in the gutters between panels; if solid panels cover more than about two thirds of the card, drop one panel rather than shrinking the lattice.
looks.imagery: The twelve cells are exactly: gold-bar-single, gold-bars-fan, gold-bars-row, gold-bars-stack, gold-bars, gold-bracelet-cuban, gold-bracelet-pair, gold-chains-pile, gold-chains, gold-class-ring, gold-coins-pile, gold-earrings-pile. Five bar shots lead the reading, then the jewellery. Optional hero cutout over the wall: gold-bracelet-cuban, gold-chains-pile, gold-bars-stack or gold-rings-scatter only. Nothing else is in the frame - no cash, no hands, no props.
neverShow: product:gold-bars (461x326 upscales 1.45x as a hero; fine as a cell, never as the big one)
ground:slab (sports-slab-graded.webp / LAB_SLAB=1 - the slab frame is Pokemon and sports only)
assort:wall|row (LAB_ASSORT must stay off; ghost walls and overlapping piles are the AI-slop read)
mark:watchMark, ringMark and the emoji ⌚ 💍 ⌚ - a watch or ring mark on a bar-led wall is a mark that does not match its picture; this theme's marks are ingot, coin, gem, sparkle, dollar only

palette:any theme id whose ink is a warm brown - the whole Sunlit family, pa01-pa03, pp01-pp03, cd01-cd03, io04, io07, io09, ik06, ik07, gl02, gl05, gl08, ck02, ck06, ck10, du02, du03, nn08, nn10, lp02, lp07 - the ink is the wash on a pale-palette tile and a brown wash under gold is mud
face:any script, handwriting, graffiti, comic or rounded face on any line
copy:an unbounded claim (beat any offer, highest prices anywhere) or a possessive on a matched competitor - WE MATCH CASH4GOLD takes no apostrophe-S
sub:watches (deckH2 GOLD WATCHES) - watch buying is the unpopular category and no theme in this collection may carry it
looks.copy: Flat, weights-and-measures voice: the number is the whole argument and nothing is decorated. Headline: "CASH FOR / GOLD" (one sentence, one face, one colour, across two lines). Selling point: "TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU". Second point: "WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE". Money line PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE with 95% set large in JetBrains Mono; kicker GOLD BUYER; CTA GET A FREE QUOTE.
variations: Spot Ticker - the 95% runs at hero size in mono and the card carries no hero cutout, so the lattice is unbroken
Violet Wash - pa04 instead of pp04: same olive wash, violet accent instead of leaf green
Stencil Kicker - GOLD BUYER stencilled small in the top gutter between two cells rather than on a plate
Challenge Card - the sd%3 competitor slot: LOWBALLED BY CASH4GOLD? over the same wall, items line still naming 10k / 14k / 18k
looks.collectionNote:
METAL WALL is the tile discipline turned on the three metal categories, and it is recognisable at a glance because in every one of the ten the metal is the only warm, reflective, photographic thing on the card. Either twelve real cutouts lie flat in the engine's 4x3 lattice (COLS 4, ROWS 3, gap 28, cell 235x322, per-cell shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur 26 / +10 / +16) under a 60-72% wash of the palette's darkest tone, or one piece is drawn 62% of the card wide with a diagonal window shadow across it. Six tile, four cast; no photograph, no scene, no cash pile, no abstract gradient, no slab frame anywhere in the collection.

THE FAMILY RULES, true of all ten: (1) not one palette carries an amber, gold, ochre, mustard, tan or brown ground, ink, accent or support - a gold-hued word dies on a gold wall and a brown wash is the mud the owner rejected - so every wash is green, olive, teal, wine, slate or indigo and every accent is green, violet, orchid, magenta, rose, vermilion, crimson or lilac; (2) numerals are always mono (JetBrains Mono or DM Mono) because this collection's copy is weights, karats, grades and percentages; (3) display faces come only from the styles that scored and that FIT names for the metals - stencil, serif, typewriter, condensed, blackletter, slab - never script, handwriting, graffiti, comic or rounded; (4) the money line is a number a seller can check (PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE / PAID ON THE SPOT, AT SPOT), never an unbounded claim; (5) no brand wordmark appears at all - BRAND_LOGO only maps vehicle words, and a US Mint or Tiffany mark on a private buyer's ad would imply an affiliation that does not exist, so the brand names live in the items line as text and nowhere else.

HOW TO TELL IT FROM THE OTHER NINE: the device collections tile phones and Macs and their palettes run cool-and-bright; the card collections own the slab frame; the vehicle collections own brand wordmarks and outdoor photography. Metal Wall owns the lattice of objects with mass, the deep felt-coloured wash, the mono numerals, and the spot-price line. Nothing here is a device, a card, a vehicle, a test strip, a hand, or a stack of cash.

AUDIT CONVENTIONS used in mustShow / neverShow: a plain string is an asset-name PREFIX and every one listed must be present. A string containing "|" is an alternation - at least one member must be the card's product. Entries prefixed "ground:", "sub:", "deckH2:", "mark:", "palette:", "face:", "copy:" are treatments checked against the record retheme_lab.mjs already exports per card (palette, family, layout, cat, faces, product, ground, deckH2, look) plus the layer table under LAB_EXPORT=1. Two engine facts do the heavy lifting and are worth stating once: the wall pool is the deck's own cuts prefixes sliced to 12, so it can never mix categories; and the hero/cast product is deck.cuts[(sd*7+3) % n], which is NOT filtered by quality - that is why every theme below names the products that may not be it.

looks.name: Jeweller's Case
looks.oneLine: The same twelve gold pieces, but the lattice sits inside a deep green or deep wine case with a serif headline and a review stack, the way a locked counter looks at closing time.
looks.groundSpec: Parent gold deck, same twelve cells as the Bar Wall - the difference is the wash. DEEP PALETTE: jw07 c1 #054e2f and jw10 c1 #6a2245 are both below lum 0.55, so the lattice is painted on the engine's neutral #eceef2 fallback and then washed with c1 itself at 0.60 (dark = c1 because lum(c1) < 0.3). That is the whole idea: the neutral under-plate keeps the gold's own highlights, and the 60% green or wine over it reads as jeweller's felt. Panels go solid at rgba(c1,0.9) with white copy, so the review cards and seal read as cards lying on the felt. jw07's lilac accent #e1c2fe and jw10's mint accent #94e994 are deliberately cool and light - on a deep case a light accent is the only thing that can out-shine the metal. Shadow, gap and cell geometry are identical to every other tile theme in the collection (gap 28, cell 235x322, shadow 0.28 / 26 / +10 / +16); do not soften them, the real drop shadow is what makes the flat lattice read as objects rather than stickers.
looks.imagery: Cells: gold-bar-single, gold-bars-fan, gold-bars-row, gold-bars-stack, gold-bars, gold-bracelet-cuban, gold-bracelet-pair, gold-chains-pile, gold-chains, gold-class-ring, gold-coins-pile, gold-earrings-pile. This is the one theme in the collection where gold-watch-luxury may appear as the hero over the wall, because its items line names Rolex and Cartier - and only as the hero, never as a repeated cell and never named in a headline.
neverShow: ground:photo (assets/bg-web/gold-* included - a Commons ring close-up is the 28% ground and this theme's identity is the case, not a photograph)
mark:more than two marks, or any mark in the middle third; on a deep case the marks are gem, chain, ingot, sparkle only
deckH2:GOLD WATCHES - a watch-led headline is out even though a watch may be the hero here
palette:any pale palette (this theme is the deep register; a pale ground turns it into the Bar Wall) and any warm-brown-ink palette
face:blackletter, script, handwriting or graffiti on the serif's line, and no curved headline longer than the money word
copy:naming a competitor with an apostrophe-S after WE MATCH, and any claim about karat or purity we cannot test in front of the seller
looks.copy: Quiet, discreet, estate-facing - the opposite of a pawn window. Headline: "CASH FOR / GOLD" in Instrument Serif. Selling point: "ESTATES HANDLED DISCREETLY". Second point: "WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE". Items line carries 10k / 14k / 18k / Cuban Links / Rolex / Cartier / Tiffany / Yurman as text only. Kicker TOP RATED, CTA GET A FREE QUOTE, and on reviewProof the stars are always five.
variations: Wine Case - jw10 instead of jw07: the wash goes from green felt to burgundy velvet, accent from lilac to mint
Hero Piece - gold-watch-luxury or gold-bracelet-cuban laid over the lattice at the lower right, the trust stack yielding to it
Arc Crown - CASH FOR arced up over GOLD; serif only, the money word stays flat
Four Reviews - reviewProof with four cards instead of three so the felt shows only in the gutters

looks.name: Cuban Cast
looks.oneLine: One Cuban bracelet drawn two thirds of the card wide with a soft window shadow falling across it, and a typewriter headline that reads like the written offer the copy promises.
looks.groundSpec: Gold pass with LAB_SUBCATS=1, the bracelets slot: deck.cuts is ['gold-bracelet'] so the hero pool is exactly gold-bracelet-cuban (1484x1184) and gold-bracelet-pair (1294x1041) - both correct, both high enough resolution that the cast never upscales (k = min(669.6/w, 993.6/h) = 0.45 and 0.52). The engine builds the ground: fill c1; on a PALE palette (cd04 c1 #91e2a2, lum 0.61) add ink at 0.20 and a linear accent 0.18 to ink 0.10 top to bottom so the mint does not stay a pastel; a white sheen gradient at 0.12 from the top left; the bracelet drawn at 0.92 alpha, translated to (0.66W, 0.52H), rotated -0.12 rad, shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.35) blur 40 offset +24/+30; then the diagonal window shadow - blur 26 at 0.58 plus a blur 60 penumbra at 0.29 - and a scrim of the ink at 0.30. On the DEEP palette (jw08 c1 #284c06) there is no ink overlay, the shadow strength drops to 0.50 and the scrim is c1 at 0.22, so the bracelet keeps more of its own light. Cast strips every Hero Product and Lineup Product layer - the product IS the ground here, and a second cutout on top is a fault, not a bonus.
looks.imagery: One object only: gold-bracelet-cuban (default) or gold-bracelet-pair. Nothing else is drawn. The chains slot (gold-chains-pile, gold-chains) is the sanctioned alternative pool if the run is pinned to chains rather than bracelets; gold-chains at 624x457 upscales 1.07x, which is the outer limit this theme accepts.
neverShow: gold-teeth-dental (gold crowns at 62% of the card is the image that loses the reader; dental stays a word in the items line)
gold-scale-weighing (the object is a white lab scale - the gold in it is a few grains and reads as an appliance at hero size)
gold-bars (461x326, 1.45x upscale as a cast hero)
ground:tile on this theme (the lattice is the sibling theme; this one is the single piece)
layer:any cutout on top of the cast (cast removes Hero Product / Lineup Product - if one survives, the card is broken)
mark:more than one mark, and any mark over the bracelet
face:Special Elite on body copy or on any line longer than the money word - the typewriter carries the headline and the money line only, Manrope carries everything else
copy:CASH FOR GOLD split across two faces or two colours; it is one sentence in one face
palette:any warm-brown-ink palette, and any palette whose accent reads gold or amber
looks.copy: A written offer, typed. Headline: "CASH FOR / GOLD" in Special Elite. Selling point: "WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE". Second point: "TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU". With the bracelets deck the money word may be GOLD BRACELETS with the spec line CUBAN, BANGLES, TENNIS; kicker WE PAY MORE; money line PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE; CTA GET A FREE QUOTE.
variations: Pair Cast - gold-bracelet-pair instead of the single Cuban, the window shadow crossing both
Olive Deep - jw08 instead of cd04: no ink overlay, the bracelet keeps its own highlights, periwinkle accent
Knockout Band - bandKnockout, CASH FOR knocked out of a solid accent band across the shadow's seam
Chains Slot - the chains sub-deck instead of bracelets: gold-chains-pile cast, headline GOLD CHAINS, spec CUBAN, ROPE, FIGARO, BYZANTINE

looks.name: Karat Counter
looks.oneLine: The gold lattice under a teal or plum wash with the karat ladder - 10k, 14k, 18k, 22k - stacked in mono down a solid panel, the wall showing through the gutters.
looks.groundSpec: Parent gold deck, the same twelve cells, deliberately washed a different temperature from its two gold siblings: pa05 washes with ink #1b4037 (deep teal-green) at 0.60 over the wall painted on c1 #c6faeb; pp09 washes with ink #443045 (plum) at 0.60 over c1 #faf3fb. Teal and plum are the two cool tones that make yellow gold look yellow rather than brown, which is the whole reason this theme exists next to the olive Bar Wall and the green-and-wine Case. Geometry as always: 4x3, gap 28, cell 235x322, shadow 0.28 / 26 / +10 / +16. Composition differs from its siblings by panel weight rather than by ground: hudTech and stepsFlow lay big solid rgba(ink,0.9) panels over the left two thirds, so only a vertical strip of the lattice is visible - the wall becomes a texture behind a spec sheet. If a run ever hands this theme a deep palette, the wall paints on #eceef2 and the wash becomes c1; that is legal but it collapses the difference with the Jeweller's Case, so keep it pale.
looks.imagery: Cells: the twelve approved gold- cutouts (five bar shots, two bracelets, two chain shots, class ring, coins pile, earrings pile). The karat ladder is typography, not imagery - do not try to letter the cells. Optional hero over the wall: gold-class-ring or gold-earrings-pile, both of which sit small and do not fight the panel.
neverShow: gold-watch-luxury (the watch belongs to the Jeweller's Case; on a karat card it is a different sale)
mark:watchMark and the ⌚ emoji; marks here are ingot, coin, gem, dollar
palette:any warm-brown-ink palette; also any palette whose ink is olive-green, which would duplicate the Bar Wall
face:Oswald on more than the headline and the ladder - Instrument Sans carries the sub lines
copy:a karat we do not test (24k jewellery claims), any unbounded price claim, and any second sentence in the headline face
looks.copy: Counter voice, itemised: what you have, what it weighs, what it pays. Headline: "CASH FOR / GOLD". Selling point: "TESTED AND WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU". Second point: "ESTATES HANDLED DISCREETLY". The ladder 10k / 14k / 18k / 22k runs down the panel in DM Mono; money line PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE; kicker GOLD BUYER; CTA GET A FREE QUOTE.

Spec Sheet - hudTech, the ladder and the three sub lines in one tall panel, the lattice as a right-hand strip
Three Steps - stepsFlow: bring it, we weigh it, you leave paid, with the wall in the gutters
Ring Hero - gold-class-ring laid at the lower right, small, the panel yielding to it

looks.name: Silver Bar Wall
looks.oneLine: Seven silver bullion cutouts tiled across twelve cells under a deep teal wash, with a vermilion headline - the only hot thing on a cold card.
looks.groundSpec: Silver pass with LAB_SUBCATS=1, the bullion slot: deck.cuts ['silver-bar','silver-coin','silver-round'] yields exactly seven approved cutouts, so the twelve cells are filled by pool[(i+seed)%7] and five objects appear twice. That repeat is deliberate and safe - at 4x3 the pairs land at cells i and i+7, which are never neighbours, so the wall reads as a stocked lattice rather than a duplication error. Wall painted on c1 (ca07 #b9f7f6, ca01 #baf8f1, both light) and washed with the ink - #173f3f / #183f3c - at 0.60. The silver cutouts are cool greys and some are tarnished, so the wash must stay dark: a pale wash leaves grey-on-grey and that is the 'too bland, what is this light theme' card. The accent is the counterweight - ca07 vermilion #d8360a, ca01 red #d9322b - and it belongs to type and rules only, never to a shape laid over the metal. Panels solid at rgba(ink,0.9), white copy. Geometry as always: gap 28, cell 235x322, shadow 0.28 / 26 / +10 / +16.
looks.imagery: The seven cells, each twice or once: silver-bar-single, silver-bars-row, silver-bars-stack, silver-bars, silver-coins-spill, silver-coins-tube, silver-rounds-pile. silver-rounds-pile is a bright pile of 90% junk-silver coins, which is exactly what the items line means by junk silver - the picture and the words agree. Optional hero over the wall: silver-bars-stack or silver-rounds-pile only.
neverShow: product:silver-flatware as a hero (364x587, 1.69x upscale) and silver-bars as a hero (519x476, 1.29x)
deckH2:STERLING SILVERWARE and deckH2:SILVER JEWELRY - in a subcats silver pass those slots also fire; this theme's cards must carry deckH2 SILVER BARS & COINS
ground:photo (assets/bg-web/silver-* is cutlery and rings, not bullion - the wrong picture for this headline)
mark:the 🏺 and 🥈 emoji from the silver set - an amphora is the rejected tea-set category and a medal is not bullion; marks here are ingot, coin, sparkle, check
palette:any warm-brown-ink palette, any gold or amber accent (it would read as the wrong metal on a silver card)
copy:the sub line that promises TEA SETS - both tea-set cutouts are rejected, so this wall cannot show one; use WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU, SPOT SHOWN and ANTIQUE AND ESTATE PIECES WELCOME
looks.copy: Cold, exact, transactional - the silver equivalent of the bar wall. Headline: "WE BUY / SILVER". Selling point: "WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU, SPOT SHOWN". Second point: "ANTIQUE AND ESTATE PIECES WELCOME". looks.name: Sterling Drawer
looks.oneLine: The full sterling drawer - flatware, candlesticks, tubes, rounds and a jewellery pile - tiled under a one-hue teal wash with a blackletter money word.
looks.groundSpec: Parent silver deck (LAB_SUBCATS=0) so the pool is all eleven approved silver- cutouts; eleven into twelve cells means exactly one object repeats, at cells i and i+11, which cannot be adjacent. Wall painted on c1 (pp06 #edf8fa, pp05 #eef9f5) and washed with the ink - #173e45 / #1d4035 - at 0.60. pp06 is a one-hue palette: accent #008394 and support #1d96a8 are two tones of the same teal, so the card is ground plus one colour in tones, which is what the owner asked for and what keeps a drawer full of tarnished objects from turning into a colour mess. pp05 is the same wash with an orchid support for a slightly warmer read. Panels solid rgba(ink,0.9). Geometry as always. The tarnish matters: several of these cutouts are genuinely dull, so keep the wash dark and the accent bright, and never lift the wall with a light scrim.
looks.imagery: The eleven cells: silver-bar-single, silver-bars-row, silver-bars-stack, silver-bars, silver-candlesticks, silver-coins-spill, silver-coins-tube, silver-flatware, silver-flatware-set, silver-jewelry-mixed, silver-rounds-pile. silver-flatware is a tied bundle of forks and spoons and silver-candlesticks a tall pair - both fill a portrait cell properly; silver-flatware-set is a wide fanned row and sits short in its cell, which is correct and should not be zoomed to compensate.
neverShow: deckH2:STERLING SILVERWARE, SILVER BARS & COINS, SILVER JEWELRY - this theme runs the parent deck, deckH2 must be SILVER, because Pirata One cannot carry a nineteen-character money word

face:Pirata One on any line other than the two-word opener and the money word (max seven characters a line), on body copy, or on a curved headline - heavy decorative faces stay short and stay flat, which is why arcCrown is not in this theme's layout list

palette:any warm-brown-ink palette, and any three-hue palette - this theme is one hue in tones
copy:the TEA SETS clause (no approved tea-set or tray image exists), any unbounded claim, and a competitor possessive after WE MATCH

Selling point: "ANTIQUE AND ESTATE PIECES WELCOME". Second point: "WEIGHED IN FRONT OF YOU, SPOT SHOWN". Items line carries Sterling / .925 / Silverware / Antiques as text; money line PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE; kicker SILVER BUYER; CTA GET A FREE QUOTE.

looks.name: Estate Jewelry Cast
looks.oneLine: One mixed pile of sterling jewellery drawn two thirds of the card wide on a deep teal jewel ground, a window shadow across it and a pink accent doing the talking.
looks.groundSpec: Silver pass with LAB_SUBCATS=1, the jewelry slot: deck.cuts ['silver-ring','silver-chain','silver-jewel'] resolves to exactly one approved cutout, silver-jewelry-mixed (2048x1681), so this cast can only ever draw the right object and can never upscale (k = 0.33). Both palettes are deep (jw05 c1 #044a51, jw06 c1 #014c44), so the engine takes the deep branch: ground filled with c1, no ink overlay, a white sheen gradient at 0.10 from the top left, the pile drawn at 0.92 alpha at (0.66W, 0.52H) rotated -0.12 rad with shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.35) blur 40 offset +24/+30, the diagonal window shadow at strength 0.50 with its blur-60 penumbra at 0.25, and a scrim of c1 at 0.22. The 0.22 scrim is light on purpose: sterling is low-contrast and anything heavier turns the pile into a grey smear. Accents are pink - jw05 #febbd3, jw06 #fdb6f2 - and they sit on type and rules, never over the metal. Cast strips the Hero Product layers; a second cutout anywhere is a fault.
looks.imagery: One object: silver-jewelry-mixed, a pile of sterling chains, rings and pendants. Nothing else in the frame. If a run is pinned to the silverware slot instead, the only acceptable hero is silver-flatware-set (1989x1919); silver-flatware at 364x587 upscales 1.69x and must be rejected.

looks.imagery: The seven cells: coin-album-pages, coin-collection-tray, coin-jar-full, coin-loose-pile, coin-rolls-paper, coin-stack, coin-stack-silver. looks.collectionNote:
METAL WALL is the tile discipline turned on the three metal categories, and it is recognisable at a glance because in every one of the ten the metal is the only warm, reflective, photographic thing on the card. Either twelve real cutouts lie flat in the engine's 4x3 lattice (COLS 4, ROWS 3, gap 28, cell 235x322, per-cell shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur 26 / +10 / +16) under a 60-72% wash of the palette's darkest tone, or one piece is drawn 62% of the card wide with a diagonal window shadow across it. Six tile, four cast; no photograph, no scene, no cash pile, no abstract gradient, no slab frame anywhere in the collection.

THE FAMILY RULES, true of all ten: (1) not one palette carries an amber, gold, ochre, mustard, tan or brown ground, ink, accent or support - a gold-hued word dies on a gold wall and a brown wash is the mud the owner rejected - so every wash is green, olive, teal, wine, slate or indigo and every accent is green, violet, orchid, magenta, rose, vermilion, crimson or lilac; (2) numerals are always mono (JetBrains Mono or DM Mono) because this collection's copy is weights, karats, grades and percentages; (3) display faces come only from the styles that scored and that FIT names for the metals - stencil, serif, typewriter, condensed, blackletter, slab - never script, handwriting, graffiti, comic or rounded; (4) the money line is a number a seller can check (PAYING 95% OF SPOT PRICE / PAID ON THE SPOT, AT SPOT), never an unbounded claim; (5) no brand wordmark appears at all - BRAND_LOGO only maps vehicle words, and a US Mint or Tiffany mark on a private buyer's ad would imply an affiliation that does not exist, so the brand names live in the items line as text and nowhere else.

HOW TO TELL IT FROM THE OTHER NINE: the device collections tile phones and Macs and their palettes run cool-and-bright; the card collections own the slab frame; the vehicle collections own brand wordmarks and outdoor photography. Metal Wall owns the lattice of objects with mass, the deep felt-coloured wash, the mono numerals, and the spot-price line. Nothing here is a device, a card, a vehicle, a test strip, a hand, or a stack of cash.

AUDIT CONVENTIONS used in mustShow / neverShow: a plain string is an asset-name PREFIX and every one listed must be present. A string containing "|" is an alternation - at least one member must be the card's product. Entries prefixed "ground:", "sub:", "deckH2:", "mark:", "palette:", "face:", "copy:" are treatments checked against the record retheme_lab.mjs already exports per card (palette, family, layout, cat, faces, product, ground, deckH2, look) plus the layer table under LAB_EXPORT=1. Two engine facts do the heavy lifting and are worth stating once: the wall pool is the deck's own cuts prefixes sliced to 12, so it can never mix categories; and the hero/cast product is deck.cuts[(sd*7+3) % n], which is NOT filtered by quality - that is why every theme below names the products that may not be it.

looks.name: Graded Case
looks.oneLine: A fan of graded coin holders drawn two thirds of the card wide under a window shadow, with a tall condensed headline and the grade line set in mono like a certificate.
looks.groundSpec: Coins pass with LAB_SUBCATS=1, the slabs slot. One caution the operator has to know: deck.cuts is ['coin-slab','coin-graded'], and the prefix 'coin-slab' catches the 144x144 coin-slab.webp as well as coin-slabs-stack, so one hero in three is a four-and-a-half-times upscale of a thumbnail. Until that prefix reads 'coin-slabs' - one letter - the audit must reject any card whose product is coin-slab. The two legitimate heroes are coin-graded-fan-three (1950x1865) and coin-slabs-stack (1849x1314), both real holders with real coins visible inside them. cd06 is pale (c1 #80dafd, lum 0.61) so the engine adds ink at 0.20 plus a magenta-to-ink gradient at 0.18, shadow strength 0.58, scrim ink #1b3d49 at 0.30; jw09 is deep (c1 #054666) so no overlay, shadow 0.50, scrim c1 at 0.22. On jw09 keep the salmon accent #fdc0b7 on the grade line, the rules and the plate - a large salmon word beside a silver coin is the one place in this collection where an accent could be mistaken for metal. Cast strips the Hero Product layers.
looks.imagery: One object: coin-graded-fan-three (three PCGS-style holders fanned, coins visible) or coin-slabs-stack (three stacked holders). Both carry BLANK white labels - that is why they are approved where the empty coin-slab-graded holder was rejected: a holder with a coin in it is a product. Never letter those blank labels with a fake grade or a grading company's name; the grade line is typography on the card, beside the holder, not on it.
neverShow: coin-slab (144x144, 4.65x upscale as a cast hero - and it is a raw coin, not a slab)

looks.name: Morgan Row

looks.groundSpec: Coins pass with LAB_SUBCATS=1, the dollars slot: deck.cuts ['coin-silver-dollar','coin-morgan'] resolves to exactly one approved cutout, coin-silver-dollar-pair (1759x1902), so the hero is guaranteed correct and never upscales (k = 0.38). Cast strips the Hero Product layers.
looks.imagery: One object: coin-silver-dollar-pair - two silver dollars, obverse and reverse, the most recognisable coin in America and the exact subject of the headline. Nothing else in the frame.

looks.name: Device Wall Proof
looks.oneLine: A flat lattice of single Apple press phones, each with its own real drop shadow, washed to 60% in the palette's dark tone, with the five-star proof block floating clear on top of it.
looks.groundSpec: The iphones.LA device wall, built by the tile branch at retheme_lab.mjs:2905. Base fill: th.c1 if its luminance is over 0.55, else th.c2 if that clears 0.55, else the neutral #eceef2 — never a mid-tone, the lattice needs a bright field to cast onto. Lattice is 4 columns x 3 rows, gap 28px, each cell scaled to 0.96 of its box so nothing touches; every cell gets shadowColor rgba(0,0,0,0.28), blur 26, offsetX 10, offsetY 16 — real shadows, no overlap, no rotation. Scrim: the palette's dark tone (c1 if lum < 0.3, else c2 if lum < 0.35, else ink) at 0.6, raised to 0.72 when that tone's own luminance is over 0.4. On a PALE palette (ca07 c1 #b9f7f6, pa05 #c6faeb) the dark tone resolves to the ink (#173f3f / #1b4037) and the wall reads as bright hardware under a deep teal wash at 0.6 — this is the target look. On a DEEP palette (cd06 c1 #80dafd is still light; if a genuinely deep palette is substituted) the wall keeps the #eceef2 field and the wash drops to c1 at 0.6 so the phones stay legible. Because the ground is busy, every stat tile and the quote card go SOLID at rgba(deep, 0.9) per the __tileBg branch at 2924 — no translucent panels on this theme.
looks.imagery: The wall is drawn only from single-unit Apple press cutouts: own-apple-cosmic-orange-02, -03, -06, -07, -10, -16, -20, own-apple-deep-blue-09, own-apple-deep-blue-18, own-apple-silver-11, own-apple-silver-15, iphone-15-pro-back-black, iphone-15-pro-back-blue, iphone-15-pro-back-gold, iphone-15-pro-back-white, iphone-15-pro-front-on, iphone-17-pro-back-black, iphone-17-pro-back-silver. Minimum 4 distinct cells required or the ground falls to cast; there are 18 candidates so it always fills. No foreground hero cutout — the wall IS the imagery, and a phone floating over the quote card would break the products-never-over-text rule.
looks.copy: Flat, factual, carrier-shaped — the seller compares a real trade-in number to what the shop paid. Headline: WE BUY iPHONES. Selling point: CRACKED OR LOCKED STILL PAID. Second selling point: WRITTEN OFFER IN MINUTES. Quote: "Carrier said $180. These guys paid $610." Signature: Marcus T. · Long Beach, CA. Rating line: 4.9 · 200+ local sellers, five stars.
variations: Quote mark — the 200px Instrument Serif opening mark in the accent rides the card's top-left gutter, quote indented 130px (the 73% winner)
Two-line strip — two rounded review rows, 942x86, name right-aligned at 980 (the 82% winner); the two quotes must be seed-offset so two cards of this theme never print the same pair
Locked-phone card — the wall swaps to the deep-blue and silver own-apple cells only and the quote becomes "iCloud was still on, they walked me through it and paid."
Named-competitor card — the line reads WE MATCH BEST BUY with best-buy.png in the free corner; the logo id must equal the name printed on the card and appears on no other variation
looks.collectionNote: PROOF WALL is ten cards that all say the same thing in the same order: five stars, a signed testimonial written in the seller's own trade vocabulary, a first name and initial with a Long Beach-area city, and — standing behind all of it — a real photograph or a real lattice of the exact goods the quote is talking about. The family signature is a three-part proof block that is always the loudest object on the card: RATING (five stars plus "4.9 · 200+ local sellers", never four, never three), QUOTE (one sentence in quotation marks from the QUOTES pool in scripts/retheme_lab.mjs, in the theme's grotesque support face, never the display face), SIGNATURE (pin + "Marcus T. · Long Beach, CA" from NAMES2/CITIES2, centred, 26px floor, charSpacing 20). Every card is built on reviewProof (93%, the best layout in the data) with at least one non-reviewProof sibling layout so that no run of this collection ever trips the REVIEW_PAGE / r100 switch at line 2672 of retheme_lab.mjs. What tells this collection apart from the other nine at a glance: the other nine sell by asserting; this one sells by quoting, and the imagery is always evidence for the quote rather than decoration around it — the scale in the ground under "weighed it in front of me", the Charizard in the slab window under "they knew what the alt arts were worth", the F-150 photograph under "lien on the truck, they sorted the payoff". The negative spine shared by all ten: no ip-gen* renders anywhere (AI fakes, ticked at thumbnail size by mistake, excluded by the LEGACY regex at line 41); no qs-iphone-* / qs-ipad-* press composites inside a tiled wall (each of those files is a two-up back-and-front, so a lattice cell holding one shows two objects); no cross-category product (a Pokemon card never wears an iPhone, a gold card never wears a coin slab frame); no watches as a theme premise; no scene-ref-*, scene-sam-*, scene-pix-*, scene-android-*, scene-allbrands-* (competitor references and non-Apple lineups); no spotlight / marble / memphis / linen grounds (the four the owner struck); no star run that is not exactly five; and no second sentence in a different face inside one headline.

looks.name: Studio Lineup Proof
looks.oneLine: An Apple press flat-lay or studio lineup under a palette tint, with the proof block sitting in the clear half of the frame and the headline naming exactly the line that is in the photograph.
looks.groundSpec: A single photograph from assets/scenes — these are Apple PRESS images and studio flat-lays, not shop photography, so the copy never says shelf, counter or storefront. Tint by luminance, not by taste: scene-flat-iphones (lum 0.526) is a LIGHT photograph and takes the palette's DARK tone at scrim 0.5; scene-studio-slate-quad (0.172), scene-own-macbook-stack (0.164) and scene-studio-amber-ipad (0.192) are dark and take th.c1 at 0.22-0.30 so the hardware still reads. Detail on every approved scene here is under 13, so none of them qualify as busy and none takes the 0.62 heavy scrim. Pick for CONTRAST with the ground, never nearest luminance — a pp04 near-white theme (#f2f8ef) on a bright flat-lay under a white scrim renders as a blank page. On a PALE palette pick a scene under lum 0.30 (scene-studio-slate-quad, scene-own-macbook-stack, scene-own-stock-studio); on a deeper palette pick one over 0.38 (scene-flat-iphones, scene-iso-ipad-cool, scene-pick-bone-flat). Copy with no plate behind it takes the over-scrim tone plus a soft carry shadow per the image-bg branch at 2943.
looks.imagery: The photograph is the imagery and it must show the line the headline names. iPHONE headline: scene-flat-iphones, scene-iso-iphone-mint, scene-iso-iphone-warm, scene-iso-iphone-grey, scene-iso-iphone-dark, scene-studio-blue-trio, scene-studio-green-trio, scene-studio-rose-pair, scene-studio-slate-quad, scene-grad-iphone-teal, scene-grad-iphone-violet, scene-grad-iphone-coral. iPAD headline: scene-flat-ipads, scene-iso-ipad-cool, scene-pick-slate-ipads, scene-studio-amber-ipad, scene-grad-ipad-mint, scene-grad-ipad-teal, scene-grad-ipad-violet. MACBOOK headline: scene-own-macbook-open, scene-own-macbook-stack, scene-grad-mac-gold. The mixed line iPHONE · iPAD · MACBOOK is the only headline allowed over scene-flat-apple-cool, scene-flat-apple-warm, scene-flat-apple-coral, scene-own-iphone-ipad-desk, scene-own-stock-studio, scene-own-stock-grad.
looks.copy: Calm and same-day; the seller measures the shop in hours, not promises. Headline: iPHONE · iPAD · MACBOOK. Selling point: WRITTEN OFFER IN MINUTES. Second selling point: CASH THE SAME DAY. Quote: "Texted photos at noon, had cash by 3pm." Signature: Priya R. · Torrance, CA.
variations: Headline top — the money line rides the top edge above the rating block (the 75% winner) and the photograph carries the lower two thirds
Mac card — scene-own-macbook-open, headline WE BUY MACBOOKS, quote "Met me at work. Five minutes, done."; the mark set drops to the macbook icons so no iPhone emoji appears on a Mac ad
iPad card — scene-flat-ipads, headline WE BUY iPADS, items line PRO, AIR, MINI
Free rating — the pill is dropped and five stars sit centred at 44px over the photograph with 4.9 AVERAGE · 200+ LOCAL SELLERS beneath (the 76% rating winner)

looks.name: Scale Counter Proof
looks.oneLine: A gold piece cast large into the ground under a soft diagonal window shadow, with the proof block on the lit side and a quote about being weighed in front of you.
looks.groundSpec: The cast branch at retheme_lab.mjs:2876. The chosen gold cutout is drawn into the ground at 62% of the width / 92% of the height, centred at (0.66W, 0.52H), rotated -0.12 rad, globalAlpha 0.92, shadowColor rgba(0,0,0,0.35) blur 40 offsetX 24 offsetY 30. Every allowed photo is dark: trucks-ford-f-150-1 (lum 0.251, detail 11.2), -2 (0.411, 17.6), -3 (0.271, 35.3); trucks-chevrolet-silverado-pickup-1 (0.171, 40.6), -3 (0.182, 34.7); vans-ford-transit-van-1 (0.138, 13.7), -2 (0.340, 13.3), -3 (0.340, 23.5); bikes-harley-davidson-motorcycle-1 (0.188, 43.7), -2 (0.259, 24.9), -3 (0.325, 36.4); cars-bmw-key-1 (0.235, 14.6), -2 (0.283, 6.8), -3 (0.091, 7.8); cars-used-car-dealership-lot-1 (0.301, 49.8); vans-cargo-van-1 (0.253, 8.4); trucks-pickup-truck-1 (0.222, 22.8), -3 (0.200, 27.8); bikes-cruiser-motorcycle-parked-1 (0.226, 13.1), -2 (0.132, 24.1). Anything with detail over 14 is BUSY: on a mid-tone palette such as du08 (#5593ef) it takes th.c1 at 0.62; on the deep jw01 (#1f3e7a) or jw05 (#044a51) it takes 0.44 so the vehicle still shows. Detail-under-14 shots (cars-bmw-key-2, vans-cargo-van-1, trucks-ford-f-150-1, vans-ford-transit-van-2) take the accent tint at 0.24-0.30 on a light palette and c1 at 0.42-0.50 on a deep one. No grayscale — vehicle photographs keep their colour under the tint.
looks.imagery: The photograph must match the card's category prefix (trucks- under a truck headline, vans- under a van headline, bikes- under a motorcycle headline, cars- under a car headline), and the brand line must match the filename: ford.png only over trucks-ford-f-150-*.jpg or vans-ford-transit-van-*.jpg; chevrolet.png only over trucks-chevrolet-silverado-pickup-1/3.jpg; harley-davidson.png only over bikes-harley-davidson-motorcycle-1/2/3.jpg; bmw.png only over cars-bmw-key-1/2/3.jpg. Unbranded photos (cars-used-car-dealership-lot-1, vans-cargo-van-1, trucks-pickup-truck-1/3, bikes-cruiser-motorcycle-parked-1/2) carry a generic money word and NO logo. Optional foreground cutout, clearing all text: car-keys, car-keys-fob, car-title-docs, car-hand-keys-over.
looks.copy: Transactional and logistical — title, lien payoff, DMV, tow, same day. The competitor is named and never given an apostrophe-S. Headline: WE BUY F-150S. Items line: F-150 · SUPER DUTY · RANGER · MAVERICK. Selling point: LIEN PAYOFF AND DMV HANDLED. Second selling point: WE COME TO YOU. Quote: "Lien on the truck, they sorted the payoff." Signature: Miguel S. · Long Beach, CA. Seal may read INSURED here — this is the only collection theme where that seal is correct.
variations: Ford card — trucks-ford-f-150-2.jpg with ford.png, headline WE BUY F-150S, items F-150 · SUPER DUTY · RANGER
Harley card — bikes-harley-davidson-motorcycle-2.jpg at scrim 0.44 with harley-davidson.png, money word WE BUY MOTORCYCLES or WE BUY HARLEYS, flame marks
Transit card — vans-ford-transit-van-2.jpg with ford.png, headline WE BUY WORK VANS, quote "Offer in ten minutes, check cleared same day."
Match card — WE MATCH CARVANA with the offer named on the following line and carmax.png or autonation.png only when that name is the one printed
looks.collectionNote: PROOF WALL is ten cards that all say the same thing in the same order: five stars, a signed testimonial written in the seller's own trade vocabulary, a first name and initial with a Long Beach-area city, and — standing behind all of it — a real photograph or a real lattice of the exact goods the quote is talking about. The family signature is a three-part proof block that is always the loudest object on the card: RATING (five stars plus "4.9 · 200+ local sellers", never four, never three), QUOTE (one sentence in quotation marks from the QUOTES pool in scripts/retheme_lab.mjs, in the theme's grotesque support face, never the display face), SIGNATURE (pin + "Marcus T. · Long Beach, CA" from NAMES2/CITIES2, centred, 26px floor, charSpacing 20). Every card is built on reviewProof (93%, the best layout in the data) with at least one non-reviewProof sibling layout so that no run of this collection ever trips the REVIEW_PAGE / r100 switch at line 2672 of retheme_lab.mjs. What tells this collection apart from the other nine at a glance: the other nine sell by asserting; this one sells by quoting, and the imagery is always evidence for the quote rather than decoration around it — the scale in the ground under "weighed it in front of me", the Charizard in the slab window under "they knew what the alt arts were worth", the F-150 photograph under "lien on the truck, they sorted the payoff". The negative spine shared by all ten: no ip-gen* renders anywhere (AI fakes, ticked at thumbnail size by mistake, excluded by the LEGACY regex at line 41); no qs-iphone-* / qs-ipad-* press composites inside a tiled wall (each of those files is a two-up back-and-front, so a lattice cell holding one shows two objects); no cross-category product (a Pokemon card never wears an iPhone, a gold card never wears a coin slab frame); no watches as a theme premise; no scene-ref-*, scene-sam-*, scene-pix-*, scene-android-*, scene-allbrands-* (competitor references and non-Apple lineups); no spotlight / marble / memphis / linen grounds (the four the owner struck); no star run that is not exactly five; and no second sentence in a different face inside one headline.

looks.name: Review Ledger Proof
looks.oneLine: Three signed reviews written down a ruled sheet, the rating struck through with one highlighter, the quote card pinned as one sticky note, and a single product cutout from the card's own category holding the page.
looks.groundSpec: The Lined Paper family owns its ground, so no photograph and no drawn device wall runs on this theme — familyGround is true and every photo pass steps aside. Sheet: paper:ruled, paper:legal, paper:grid or paper:dots at scrim 0.001, cream (lp01 #ecf4fd, lp05 #e9f7f7, lp09 #eaf7f2). On a ruled or legal sheet every single-line text object is baseline-snapped to the 54px rule grid from a 150px top (130 on legal) and non-headline rows are capped at 40px so they sit between the rules. Exactly ONE highlighter colour and ONE sticky colour per card: bands and pills 200px+ wide and 210px or shorter become a highlighter stroke at 0.55 opacity, rx 0.18h, rotated under a degree, with a fainter 0.3 overrun stroke behind it so the ends run past like a real marker; larger cards and panels become sticky notes at 0.96 opacity, rx 4, tilted 1.2 degrees, shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.22) blur 22 offset 4/10; boxes under 130px square take the pen colour solid. Headlines alternate pen accent and #26231f ink with a 1.2-degree hand-set tilt; every sheen, vignette and grain layer is switched off. Marks are drawn in pen ink, never emoji. Because this ground is pale by construction there is no deep variant: the body comes from the pen accent and the sticky, not from a scrim.
looks.imagery: One product cutout, and it must belong to the card's own category: phones takes own-apple-cosmic-orange-02/-06/-10, own-apple-deep-blue-09, own-apple-silver-11, iphone-15-pro-back-blue or iphone-17-pro-back-black; gold takes gold-chains-pile, gold-bracelet-cuban, gold-rings-scatter or gold-bars-stack; coins takes coin-rolls-paper, coin-jar-full, coin-album-pages or coin-stack; pokemon takes poke-slabs-trio (the only approved Pokemon cutout); strips takes strip-boxes, strip-boxes-fan or strip-kit-meter. checklist-clipboard and receipt-paper-curl may join as a second element but never stand alone as the card's only imagery — a prop is not a product.
looks.copy: Handwritten in look only — every word is set type. Three short reviews down the page, each signed, with the money word for the card's own category at the top. Headline: SELL YOUR GOLD. Selling point: FREE WRITTEN OFFER BEFORE YOU DECIDE. Second selling point: NO LOWBALL "FINAL OFFERS". Quote: "Quote in writing before I decided. Took it." Signature: Lena P. · Lakewood, CA. Rating: five stars struck through with the single highlighter, 4.9 · 200+ local sellers beside it.
variations: Ruled sheet — paper:ruled, three review rows snapped to the 54px grid, quotes seed-offset so no two cards of this theme open with the same sentence
Legal pad — paper:legal with the money word tilted 1.2 degrees and the sticky note carrying one long quote instead of three short ones
Grid sheet — paper:grid for the phones and strips cards, where the squared paper reads as an inventory count
Pen-mark set — the category's own marks drawn in the pen accent at 84px in two corners, no emoji, per the Lined Paper family rule

looks.name: Counter White
looks.oneLine: A near-white card with one teal-blue accent, the real meter-and-case kit lying large in the ground under a soft window shadow, and the whole offer set in plain grotesque with mono numbers.
looks.groundSpec: Chalk ck03 ground #f2f8f9 (lum 0.94, so the pale branch fires): fill c1, then ink #173f43 at 0.20 over the whole field, then a top-to-bottom gradient of accent #026a73 at 0.18 down to ink at 0.10. strip-kit-meter is drawn at 0.62W, centred at 0.66W / 0.52H, rotated -0.12 rad, shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.35) blur 40 offset 24/30, alpha 0.92. Then the diagonal window shadow: blur(26px) rgba(8,10,16,0.58) from 0.62W to 0.22W, plus a blur(60px) penumbra at half strength. Scrim: because c2 #e4dedf is pale (lum 0.85, not < 0.45) the tint falls to ink #173f43 at 0.30 — a dark teal wash that will hold white type. Panels then go solid at ink 0.9 with white copy. ON ck09 (#f3f8fa, accent #0c658d) the same numbers hold; only the gradient hue moves to indigo. This theme has no deep palette — if it is ever run on one, the pale branch drops out, the ink wash and accent gradient are skipped, and the scrim becomes c1 at 0.22, which is too light to carry the review stack, so do not do it.
looks.imagery: assets/cutouts/strip-kit-meter.webp only — the grey-and-white meter with a test strip in its slot, sitting in its open zip case with the closed case beside it. Nothing else is drawn into the ground. The category mark is check or shield, placed in a free corner clear of every word.
neverShow: a brand name in the headline (this meter is a generic unit, not OneTouch or Contour — only DIABETIC SUPPLIES, TEST STRIPS or GLUCOSE METERS may sit over it)
the drop and vial marks and the 🩸 and 🧪 emoji
the Chalk support tone #382221 used as a panel or band fill — it reads brown
graffiti, script, handwritten, blackletter, comic, horror and novelty faces
looks.copy: Plain, unhurried, pharmacy-counter voice — no exclamation, no urgency words, nothing bolder than the facts. Headline: CASH FOR / DIABETIC SUPPLIES (one sentence, one face, one weight, one colour). Selling point: SEALED, IN-DATE BOXES ONLY. Kicker STRIP BUYER; items line OneTouch • FreeStyle • Contour • Accu-Chek • Dexcom Sensors • In-Date Sealed; money line TOP BOX PRICES PAID; CTA GET YOUR OFFER; sticker PAID TODAY.
variations: Teal (ck03) — the default, accent #026a73.
Indigo (ck09) — accent #0c658d, the only change.
Shadow off — the diagonal window shadow drops to 0.40 strength so the meter reads brighter on the reviewProof layout, where the quote card already darkens the left.
Mark swap — shield instead of check on trustSeal, so the seal and the mark are not the same shape twice.
looks.collectionNote:
CLINIC is the pale, cool, quiet collection: ten cards you would believe were printed by a pharmacy. Every one sits on a near-white or pale-cool ground (one deep exception), carries exactly ONE cool accent in tones — medical blue, teal or clinic green, never magenta, violet, mustard or brown — and sets its numbers in a monospace face (JetBrains Mono / DM Mono). That mono numeral is the collection's fingerprint: lot numbers, box counts, expiry dates. No graffiti, script, handwriting, blackletter, comic, horror or novelty faces appear anywhere in this collection, which is what separates it at a glance from the card-shop, gold and vehicle collections. Copy is factual and discreet: SEALED, IN-DATE BOXES ONLY / LOCAL PICKUP OR PREPAID MAIL-IN / PAID THE DAY WE RECEIVE THEM.

FIVE VERIFIED FACTS THIS COLLECTION IS BUILT ON — I opened every file and looked at every image:

1. TILE IS IMPOSSIBLE FOR STRIPS. The tile wall needs pool.length >= 4 (retheme_lab.mjs ~line 2900). The approved strip cutouts are only four — strip-boxes-fan, strip-boxes-pile-large, strip-boxes, strip-kit-meter — and the MULTI regex drops -fan, leaving THREE. The 100%-approval ground cannot be built for this category today. No theme here declares `tile`; declaring it would silently render a `cast` instead (dgKinds falls through). Every theme names the ground it will actually get.

2. TWO OF THE FOUR APPROVED STRIP CUTOUTS ARE NOT DIABETIC SUPPLIES. I converted and viewed them. `strip-boxes-fan` is a fan of BLANK WHITE BOXES plus a lateral-flow rapid-test cassette printed C / T / S / ID: — the owner rejected `strip-boxes-cash` and `strip-vials-pile` under reason "not-diabetes" and rejected `strip-box-single`, `strip-boxes-row-five`, `strip-boxes-stack`, `strip-box-open-vials` under "blank-unbranded", and this file is both of those things at once. `strip-boxes-pile-large` is a pile of PLAIN KRAFT CARDBOARD CUBES — literally the "kraft cartons… nothing says what is bought" he rejected. Both are ticked APPROVED (same thumbnail-size mistake as ip-gen17) and both are live in CUTS.strips today, so a `cast` card has a ~50% chance of drawing a kraft cube or a pregnancy-test-shaped cassette as its hero under CASH FOR TEST STRIPS. Every theme below bans both by name. The only honest strip cutouts are `strip-kit-meter` (a real meter with a strip in the slot, in its zip case) and `strip-boxes` (a fan of loose strips with gold contact bars).

3. THE freestyle-libre LOGO IS THE ABBOTT CORPORATE MARK. assets/logos/ATTRIBUTION.json names it "File:Abbott_Laboratories_logo.svg" and the PNG is the cyan 'a' symbol beside a black "Abbott" wordmark — not a FreeStyle Libre mark. And assets/bg-web/strips-freestyle-libre-3.jpg is a DEXCOM G6 worn sensor (the wordmark is legible in frame) filed under a FreeStyle Libre filename, on skin, with body hair and dried blood under the adhesive. Naming Libre over that photo is a brand lie on top of an ugly picture; it is banned collection-wide. Separately, dexcom.png carries its own second line, "CONTINUOUS GLUCOSE MONITORING", so no card showing it may also print that phrase — that would be a line repeat.

4. THE BEST IMAGERY IS MISSING FROM backdrop-lum.json. The three Contour Next photographs — a real blue-and-white Contour Next bottle on warm-grey seamless — have no row in assets/backdrop-lum.json, so the engine assumes lum 0.3. I measured them: 0.636, 0.581, 0.650. They are BRIGHT, so the standing rule "a light photograph takes the palette's dark tone as its tint" is silently not firing on them; they fall to the accent branch at scrim 0.24 and wash out under small type. Every photo theme below states the dark tint at 0.50 explicitly.

5. THE PHOTO POOL IS UNFILTERED. WEBBG.strips is all ten strips photos picked by `pool[(sd*5+1)%pool.length]`, so a theme named for Contour can land on the OneTouch bottle, or on the bloodied-fingertip meter shots (strips-blood-glucose-meter-1 / -4). Each brand-named theme below carries an explicit photo whitelist as its mustShow and the rest as neverShow.

TWO ONE-LINE ENGINE CHANGES THIS COLLECTION NEEDS, neither of which I made (analysis only): (a) `look.ground` is only honoured for 'cast' and 'tile' at line 2852 — 'photo', 'paper' and 'deep' fall through, so the photo themes will render as cast ~60% of the time until that test is widened; (b) BRAND_LOGO (line 2472) maps vehicle words only, so DEXCOM never reaches the dexcom mark — it needs `DEXCOM:'dexcom'` plus a BRAND_ITEMS entry so the headline word sets __brandWord.

Also deliberately dropped: FIT.strips currently rotates in 'hand' and 'rounded', the two worst-scoring face styles (20-22%); every theme here locks its faces, which overrides FIT entirely. Pastel is absent despite its 62% score because Pastel's construction (rel:155) puts a magenta or violet accent opposite every mint ground — the exact jumble the owner complained about. The slab frame is Pokemon and sports only, and assets/scenes/* are Apple press images, so neither appears anywhere in this collection.

looks.name: Contour Blue
looks.oneLine: The real Contour Next bottle photographed on warm-grey seamless, tinted with the palette's dark teal-blue, under a headline that names the brand in the picture.
looks.groundSpec: Ground is one of the three Contour Next photographs, full bleed. They are missing from assets/backdrop-lum.json, so the engine defaults them to lum 0.3 and picks the wrong branch — they actually measure 0.636 / 0.581 / 0.650. Force the bright-photo rule by hand: scrimColor = the palette's dark tone (pp06 ink #173e45; pp07 ink #253a4e), scrim 0.50, blur 0, treat left off. That is the standing rule 'a light photograph takes the palette's dark tone as its tint' applied where the data file cannot fire it. detail is low (a bottle on seamless, no macro texture), so no extra blur is needed and the 'busy' 0.62 wash would kill the label. Copy sits left, the bottle stays right of 0.58W, and no line may cross the blue Contour Next label — the label IS the imagery. On pp06 (mono, #edf8fa ground, accent #008394, support #1d96a8) the card is one teal-blue in tones; on pp07 (#eff7fe, accent #0378c7) it is a truer medical blue and the warm terracotta support #c0765f is forbidden as a fill. No deep palette on this theme: a deep ground under a 0.50 dark tint leaves the bottle unreadable.
looks.imagery: assets/bg-web/strips-contour-next-test-strips-1.jpg (bottle plus one loose strip), -2.jpg (bottle alone, the cleanest brand read) or -3.jpg (open bottle, strips visible inside). Nothing else. No cutout hero is added — the photograph is the product.
mustShow: the word CONTOUR in the headline
neverShow: the words ONETOUCH, FREESTYLE, LIBRE, DEXCOM or ACCU-CHEK anywhere except inside the multi-brand items line
the review quote 'Dexcom sensors too. Did not know that was a thing.' — it names the wrong brand for this card
the drop and vial marks and the 🩸 and 🧪 emoji
graffiti, script, handwritten, blackletter, comic, horror and novelty faces
looks.copy: Names the thing in the photograph and nothing else. Headline: WE BUY / CONTOUR NEXT. Selling point: PAID THE DAY WE RECEIVE THEM. Kicker STRIP BUYER; items line OneTouch • FreeStyle • Contour • Accu-Chek • Dexcom Sensors • In-Date Sealed (the only place other brands may appear); money line TOP BOX PRICES PAID; CTA GET YOUR OFFER.
variations: Bottle alone (-2) — the tightest brand read, for reviewProof where the quote card takes the left half.
Bottle and strip (-1) — the loose strip beside the bottle explains the product to someone who has never seen one.
Open bottle (-3) — strips visible inside; use only with the generic h2 TEST STRIPS, because the label is turned away and the brand is not legible.
Tint depth — 0.50 default, 0.44 on pp07 where the lighter blue ink needs the photo brighter under it.

looks.name: OneTouch Green
looks.oneLine: The black OneTouch Select Plus bottle spilling its green-and-white strips, on a near-white card whose single accent is the same clinic green as the strips.
looks.groundSpec: Ground is strips-blood-glucose-test-strips-2.jpg (lum 0.616, detail 13.22) or -3.jpg (lum 0.551, detail 15.64), full bleed. -2 sits just under the busy threshold of 14 and -3 sits just over it, so they take different washes and must be specified separately: -2 takes the bright-photo rule, scrimColor = the palette's dark tone (pp04 ink #2e3d25; io02 ink #2a3e28) at 0.50; -3 is busy, so it takes scrimColor = c1 (#f2f8ef / #e6f6e4) at 0.62, which flattens the hard blue shadow in that frame and stops the small type sitting on speckle. Both palettes are mono, so the card is one green in tones — pp04 accent #4a8704 support #599a1c, io02 accent #1e9b12 support #3e9736 — chosen because the OneTouch strips are themselves green and white: the accent and the product are the same colour on purpose. Copy goes top-left over the empty ground of the photo; the bottle and the strip spill stay lower-right. On a deep palette the 0.62 c1 wash would invert to a dark smear over a dark bottle, so this theme stays pale only.
looks.imagery: assets/bg-web/strips-blood-glucose-test-strips-2.jpg or -3.jpg — the black OneTouch Select Plus vial with its cap off and green-labelled strips spilling out. No cutout hero.

looks.collectionNote:
CLINIC is the pale, cool, quiet collection: ten cards you would believe were printed by a pharmacy. Every one sits on a near-white or pale-cool ground (one deep exception), carries exactly ONE cool accent in tones — medical blue, teal or clinic green, never magenta, violet, mustard or brown — and sets its numbers in a monospace face (JetBrains Mono / DM Mono). That mono numeral is the collection's fingerprint: lot numbers, box counts, expiry dates. No graffiti, script, handwriting, blackletter, comic, horror or novelty faces appear anywhere in this collection, which is what separates it at a glance from the card-shop, gold and vehicle collections. Copy is factual and discreet: SEALED, IN-DATE BOXES ONLY / LOCAL PICKUP OR PREPAID MAIL-IN / PAID THE DAY WE RECEIVE THEM.

FIVE VERIFIED FACTS THIS COLLECTION IS BUILT ON — I opened every file and looked at every image:

1. TILE IS IMPOSSIBLE FOR STRIPS. The tile wall needs pool.length >= 4 (retheme_lab.mjs ~line 2900). The approved strip cutouts are only four — strip-boxes-fan, strip-boxes-pile-large, strip-boxes, strip-kit-meter — and the MULTI regex drops -fan, leaving THREE. The 100%-approval ground cannot be built for this category today. No theme here declares `tile`; declaring it would silently render a `cast` instead (dgKinds falls through). Every theme names the ground it will actually get.

2. TWO OF THE FOUR APPROVED STRIP CUTOUTS ARE NOT DIABETIC SUPPLIES. I converted and viewed them. `strip-boxes-fan` is a fan of BLANK WHITE BOXES plus a lateral-flow rapid-test cassette printed C / T / S / ID: — the owner rejected `strip-boxes-cash` and `strip-vials-pile` under reason "not-diabetes" and rejected `strip-box-single`, `strip-boxes-row-five`, `strip-boxes-stack`, `strip-box-open-vials` under "blank-unbranded", and this file is both of those things at once. `strip-boxes-pile-large` is a pile of PLAIN KRAFT CARDBOARD CUBES — literally the "kraft cartons… nothing says what is bought" he rejected. Both are ticked APPROVED (same thumbnail-size mistake as ip-gen17) and both are live in CUTS.strips today, so a `cast` card has a ~50% chance of drawing a kraft cube or a pregnancy-test-shaped cassette as its hero under CASH FOR TEST STRIPS. Every theme below bans both by name. The only honest strip cutouts are `strip-kit-meter` (a real meter with a strip in the slot, in its zip case) and `strip-boxes` (a fan of loose strips with gold contact bars).

3. THE freestyle-libre LOGO IS THE ABBOTT CORPORATE MARK. assets/logos/ATTRIBUTION.json names it "File:Abbott_Laboratories_logo.svg" and the PNG is the cyan 'a' symbol beside a black "Abbott" wordmark — not a FreeStyle Libre mark. And assets/bg-web/strips-freestyle-libre-3.jpg is a DEXCOM G6 worn sensor (the wordmark is legible in frame) filed under a FreeStyle Libre filename, on skin, with body hair and dried blood under the adhesive. Naming Libre over that photo is a brand lie on top of an ugly picture; it is banned collection-wide. Separately, dexcom.png carries its own second line, "CONTINUOUS GLUCOSE MONITORING", so no card showing it may also print that phrase — that would be a line repeat.

4. THE BEST IMAGERY IS MISSING FROM backdrop-lum.json. The three Contour Next photographs — a real blue-and-white Contour Next bottle on warm-grey seamless — have no row in assets/backdrop-lum.json, so the engine assumes lum 0.3. I measured them: 0.636, 0.581, 0.650. They are BRIGHT, so the standing rule "a light photograph takes the palette's dark tone as its tint" is silently not firing on them; they fall to the accent branch at scrim 0.24 and wash out under small type. Every photo theme below states the dark tint at 0.50 explicitly.

5. THE PHOTO POOL IS UNFILTERED. WEBBG.strips is all ten strips photos picked by `pool[(sd*5+1)%pool.length]`, so a theme named for Contour can land on the OneTouch bottle, or on the bloodied-fingertip meter shots (strips-blood-glucose-meter-1 / -4). Each brand-named theme below carries an explicit photo whitelist as its mustShow and the rest as neverShow.

TWO ONE-LINE ENGINE CHANGES THIS COLLECTION NEEDS, neither of which I made (analysis only): (a) `look.ground` is only honoured for 'cast' and 'tile' at line 2852 — 'photo', 'paper' and 'deep' fall through, so the photo themes will render as cast ~60% of the time until that test is widened; (b) BRAND_LOGO (line 2472) maps vehicle words only, so DEXCOM never reaches the dexcom mark — it needs `DEXCOM:'dexcom'` plus a BRAND_ITEMS entry so the headline word sets __brandWord.

Also deliberately dropped: FIT.strips currently rotates in 'hand' and 'rounded', the two worst-scoring face styles (20-22%); every theme here locks its faces, which overrides FIT entirely. Pastel is absent despite its 62% score because Pastel's construction (rel:155) puts a magenta or violet accent opposite every mint ground — the exact jumble the owner complained about. The slab frame is Pokemon and sports only, and assets/scenes/* are Apple press images, so neither appears anywhere in this collection.

looks.name: Strip Cast
looks.oneLine: A fan of loose test strips, gold contacts and all, cast large into a pale teal ground under a diagonal window shadow, with the offer set in a single condensed voice.
looks.groundSpec: io08 ground #dbf7f6 (lum 0.90, pale branch): c1 fill, ink #173f3f at 0.20, then a vertical gradient of accent #169292 at 0.18 to ink at 0.10. strip-boxes is drawn at 0.62W centred at 0.66W / 0.52H, rotated -0.12 rad, shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.35) blur 40 offset 24/30 — the drop shadow is what makes the clear plastic sleeves read as objects rather than as a pattern. Diagonal window shadow at 0.58, penumbra at 0.29. Scrim falls to ink #173f3f at 0.30 because c2 #c1e0e3 is pale. io10 (#def7ec, accent #109672) is the same build one step greener. Both palettes are mono, so the card is one teal in tones and Oswald sets both the headline and the money number — the one place in this collection where the numerals are not mono, because a condensed figure is what a price band wants. On a deep palette the pale branch drops and the strips lose their shadow against the ground; do not run it deep.
looks.imagery: assets/cutouts/strip-boxes.webp only — the fan of individually sleeved test strips with black-and-gold electrode bars at one end. It is unbranded, which is why this theme carries only the generic headline and lets the items line name the brands.
neverShow: any brand name in the headline — this cutout carries no label, so ONETOUCH, CONTOUR, FREESTYLE, LIBRE and DEXCOM may appear only inside the items line
the drop and vial marks and the 🩸 and 🧪 emoji
graffiti, script, handwritten, blackletter, comic, horror and novelty faces
