variations: io08 teal — the default.
io10 green — accent #109672, a half-step warmer.
Low cast — the strips drop to 0.52W and sit lower, leaving the top third clear for arcCrown's curve.
Number in Oswald — the money line takes the display face rather than the mono, used on checklistHero where the price band is the widest element.

looks.name: Log Grid
looks.oneLine: A blue-ruled graph sheet, the kind a glucose log is kept on, with the offer typed onto it in Special Elite and the numbers set in mono.
looks.groundSpec: Family ground: an lp* palette makes familyGround true and the sheet is drawn, not photographed. Pin the sheet to paper:grid — ground #f7f9fb with a #b9cbe2 grid at 48px — which is the graph paper a reading log is kept on; paper:ruled, paper:legal and paper:dots are the wrong stationery for this theme. Sheet scrim is 0.001, so the paper keeps its own colour. The Lined Paper family treatment then converts panels to sticky notes and bands to highlighter, and BOTH colour arrays are fixed pastels the palette does not control: HIGHLIGHT ['#fff59d','#ffd6e7','#c9f5c4','#cfe8ff','#ffe0b3','#e8d7ff'] and STICKY ['#fff3a0','#ffd9e6','#d3f7d0','#d6ebff','#ffe4bf']. Pin both to the cool entries — highlighter #cfe8ff, sticky #d6ebff or #d3f7d0 — or the card lands a pink sticky note on a clinical sheet, which is the jumble the owner named. Small boxes take the pen colour (lp05 accent #06585c, lp01 accent #084f88); the hand-set tilt stays at ±0.8 rad on the highlighter and ±1.2 on the sticky, no more. The locked faces override the family's handwriting pool entirely — this sheet is typed, not written. There is no deep variant: the drawn sheet is always pale.
looks.imagery: assets/cutouts/strip-kit-meter.webp, small, taped to the sheet at about 0.34W in the lower right with the family's drop shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.22) blur 22 offset 4/10 — a meter clipped to a log page. The mark is clock or check in pen colour; the family drops emoji on paper, which is correct here.
neverShow: the pink and orange highlighter entries #ffd6e7, #ffe0b3, #e8d7ff and the pink and orange sticky entries #ffd9e6, #ffe4bf
the Lined Paper handwriting faces — Permanent Marker, Kalam, Cabin Sketch, Amatic SC, Gloria Hallelujah, Shadows Into Light, Nanum Pen Script, Architects Daughter, Patrick Hand
a brand name in the headline
the drop and vial marks and the 🩸 and 🧪 emoji
looks.copy: Reads like a note left on a chart: short, ordered, no adjectives. Headline: CASH FOR / TEST STRIPS & CGMS. Selling point: NO MAIL IT IN AND WAIT WEEKS. Kicker STRIP BUYER; the three-step flow is COUNT THE BOXES / SEND A PHOTO / GET PAID; CTA GET YOUR OFFER.
variations: lp05 sky — pen #06585c, highlighter #cfe8ff.
lp01 indigo — pen #084f88, sticky #d6ebff.
No tape — the meter sits unshadowed and flat on the sheet for stepsFlow, where three numbered squares already carry the depth.
Wider grid — 64px instead of 48px on trustSeal, so the seal row is not fighting the ruling.

looks.name: Mail-In Beat
looks.oneLine: The one loud card in the family: an official electric-blue ground, the meter cast into it, and a knockout band that says we beat what the mail-in sites pay.
looks.groundSpec: ck05 ground #f5f7fb (lum 0.96, pale branch): c1 fill, ink #2c3850 at 0.20, then a gradient of accent #123cef at 0.18 down to ink at 0.10 — the electric blue reads as official notice rather than as decoration. strip-kit-meter cast at 0.62W / 0.66W / 0.52H / -0.12 rad, shadow blur 40 offset 24/30, window shadow 0.58 with a 0.29 penumbra, scrim ink #2c3850 at 0.30. The knockout band takes the accent full strength and sizes to the word, never full bleed — a full-bleed band under two words is a slab. ca07 is the alternate and the only warm accent in the whole collection: ground #b9f7f6 mint with accent #d8360a, used deliberately as a single alarm red on a mint field, one band only, never as a second fill and never on the items line. On ca07 the support #1b966c green is forbidden as a fill so the card does not become mint plus red plus green. Do not run this theme deep: the pale branch is what gives the accent gradient its authority.
looks.imagery: assets/cutouts/strip-kit-meter.webp cast into the ground. No photograph — a mail-in comparison card must not show a competitor's packaging or a stock parcel. Mark is shield or dollar.
neverShow: any named competitor other than the deck's own THE MAIL-IN SITES / THE OTHER BUYERS / A MAIL-IN SITE / A RESELLER
an apostrophe-S after a competitor name
any unbounded claim such as 'we beat any offer'
a brand name in the headline
the drop and vial marks and the 🩸 and 🧪 emoji
graffiti, script, handwritten, blackletter, comic, horror and novelty faces
looks.copy: Confident, specific, never boastful — it names who it beats and what the difference is. Headline: WE BEAT / MAIL-IN OFFERS. Selling point: NO FEES THAT SHRINK YOUR PAYOUT. Kicker LOWBALLED BY A MAIL-IN SITE?; money line MORE THAN THE MAIL-IN SITES, PAID SAME DAY; CTA GET YOUR OFFER; sticker SAME DAY.
variations: Blue notice (ck05) — accent #123cef, the default and the calmer of the two.
Alarm (ca07) — mint ground, one red band, used on bandKnockout only.
Band to the word — the knockout sizes to MAIL-IN OFFERS and stops, with 24px of air each side.
Quote lead (reviewProof) — the review 'No mail-in wait. Same day.' carries the top and the band drops to a single line.

looks.name: Supply Stencil
looks.oneLine: A supply-room card: the meter cast into a pale teal ground and the headline cut in stencil, with bracket ticks instead of plates so nothing softens it.
looks.groundSpec: pp05 ground #eef9f5 (lum 0.95, pale branch): c1 fill, ink #1d4035 at 0.20, gradient of accent #16886d at 0.18 to ink at 0.10. strip-kit-meter cast at 0.62W / 0.66W / 0.52H / -0.12 rad with the standard blur-40 shadow, window shadow 0.58 and penumbra 0.29, scrim ink at 0.30. ik06 is the alternate: ground #fbedea, a pale warm off-white, with a mono teal accent #058073 and support #089485, and it carries Ink Pop's PL.ticks plate — no plate at all, just bracket ticks — which is why this theme is the crispest in the family. On a deep palette the stencil counters close up against a dark field, so this theme stays pale.

neverShow: the stencil face on any line of more than three words
the stencil face on a curve or arc
the stencil face on body copy, the items line or the phone number
a brand name in the headline — this meter carries no brand
the pp05 mauve support #a878b0 as a fill
the drop and vial marks and the 🩸 and 🧪 emoji

looks.groundSpec: Family ground again, so an lp* palette is required, but pinned to paper:ruled — cream #fbf7ea, blue rule #9fb9df at 54px, top margin at 150px, a #e08f8f margin line and punched holes. Pin the highlighter to #cfe8ff and the sticky to #d3f7d0 (lp09's green pen) or #d6ebff (lp03) — the pink and orange entries in both fixed arrays are banned. Pen colour is lp09 accent #0c5b46 or lp03 accent #055e17; small boxes take the pen, bands become a 0.55-opacity highlighter with ±0.8 rad tilt, panels become a 0.96 sticky note with a rgba(0,0,0,0.22) blur-22 offset-4/10 shadow and ±1.2 rad tilt. The locked slab face overrides the family handwriting pool entirely. No deep variant — the sheet is drawn and always cream.

the Lined Paper handwriting faces — Permanent Marker, Kalam, Cabin Sketch, Amatic SC, Gloria Hallelujah, Shadows Into Light, Nanum Pen Script, Architects Daughter, Patrick Hand
the lp09 coral support #f24f6a and the lp03 pink support #e553a3 as fills
a brand name in the headline

2. TWO OF THE FOUR APPROVED STRIP CUTOUTS ARE NOT DIABETIC SUPPLIES. I converted and viewed them. `strip-boxes-fan` is a fan of BLANK WHITE BOXES plus a lateral-flow rapid-test cassette printed C / T / S / ID: — the owner rejected `strip-boxes-cash` and `strip-vials-pile` under reason "not-diabetes" and rejected `strip-box-single`, `strip-boxes-row-five`, `strip-boxes-stack`, `strip-box-open-vials` under "blank-unbranded", and this file is both of those things at once. `strip-boxes-pile-large` is a pile of PLAIN KRAFT CARDBOARD CUBES — literally the "kraft cartons… nothing says what is bought" he rejected. Both are ticked APPROVED (same thumbnail-size mistake as ip-gen17) and both are live in CUTS.strips today, so a `cast` card has a ~50% chance of drawing a kraft cube or a pregnancy-test-shaped cassette as its hero under CASH FOR TEST STRIPS. Every theme below bans both by name. The only honest strip cutouts are `strip-kit-meter` (a real meter with a strip in the slot, in its zip case) and `strip-boxes` (a fan of loose strips with gold contact bars).

3. THE freestyle-libre LOGO IS THE ABBOTT CORPORATE MARK. assets/logos/ATTRIBUTION.json names it "File:Abbott_Laboratories_logo.svg" and the PNG is the cyan 'a' symbol beside a black "Abbott" wordmark — not a FreeStyle Libre mark. And assets/bg-web/strips-freestyle-libre-3.jpg is a DEXCOM G6 worn sensor (the wordmark is legible in frame) filed under a FreeStyle Libre filename, on skin, with body hair and dried blood under the adhesive. Naming Libre over that photo is a brand lie on top of an ugly picture; it is banned collection-wide. Separately, dexcom.png carries its own second line, "CONTINUOUS GLUCOSE MONITORING", so no card showing it may also print that phrase — that would be a line repeat.

4. THE BEST IMAGERY IS MISSING FROM backdrop-lum.json. The three Contour Next photographs — a real blue-and-white Contour Next bottle on warm-grey seamless — have no row in assets/backdrop-lum.json, so the engine assumes lum 0.3. I measured them: 0.636, 0.581, 0.650. They are BRIGHT, so the standing rule "a light photograph takes the palette's dark tone as its tint" is silently not firing on them; they fall to the accent branch at scrim 0.24 and wash out under small type. Every photo theme below states the dark tint at 0.50 explicitly.

5. THE PHOTO POOL IS UNFILTERED. WEBBG.strips is all ten strips photos picked by `pool[(sd*5+1)%pool.length]`, so a theme named for Contour can land on the OneTouch bottle, or on the bloodied-fingertip meter shots (strips-blood-glucose-meter-1 / -4). Each brand-named theme below carries an explicit photo whitelist as its mustShow and the rest as neverShow.

TWO ONE-LINE ENGINE CHANGES THIS COLLECTION NEEDS, neither of which I made (analysis only): (a) `look.ground` is only honoured for 'cast' and 'tile' at line 2852 — 'photo', 'paper' and 'deep' fall through, so the photo themes will render as cast ~60% of the time until that test is widened; (b) BRAND_LOGO (line 2472) maps vehicle words only, so DEXCOM never reaches the dexcom mark — it needs `DEXCOM:'dexcom'` plus a BRAND_ITEMS entry so the headline word sets __brandWord.

Also deliberately dropped: FIT.strips currently rotates in 'hand' and 'rounded', the two worst-scoring face styles (20-22%); every theme here locks its faces, which overrides FIT entirely. Pastel is absent despite its 62% score because Pastel's construction (rel:155) puts a magenta or violet accent opposite every mint ground — the exact jumble the owner complained about. The slab frame is Pokemon and sports only, and assets/scenes/* are Apple press images, so neither appears anywhere in this collection.

(5) The ground is always real product photography: a tiled wall of single units, a cast hero under the diagonal window shadow, or the graded-slab window — never an abstract gradient, never a bokeh vibe shot, and exactly one theme in ten is allowed a Commons photograph (bg-web scored 28%). (6) At least two selling-point lines set small and tight in one left-ranged column under the money word — the poster's small print. (7) ONE sticker, rotated 4-8deg, from CASH TODAY / PAID TODAY / SAME DAY / ON THE SPOT, in a corner, never over the money word or the product. Layout discipline is collection-wide: only the nine structural layouts (reviewProof 93, stepsFlow 58, trustSeal 55, checklistHero 53, neonNight 50, hudTech 36, bandKnockout 36, voltStack 30, lowerThird 23) are permitted; gradientWave, arcCrown, glassCard, scriptRetro, bubblePop and ticketStub are banned from all ten because a curve, a bubble, a script or a rounded stub is the opposite of a paste-up. HOW YOU TELL IT FROM THE OTHER NINE: it is the only collection where the money word breaks 240px, the only one where every card carries a full-bleed hard-edged band and a rotated sticker, and the only one with no rounded corner and no gradient on it anywhere. Two structural facts drove the category list: the Pokemon cutout pool contains exactly one approved file and it is three BLANK pastel slabs, and the sports pool contains two of which only sports-slab shows a real card face — so cards get the slab frame and the real Charizard photograph rather than a wall, and iPad is deliberately absent because every approved qs-ipad-* file is a two-up composite that destroys a lattice.

looks.oneLine: A pale dealer board tiled with the wordmarks of the thirteen makes we buy, one marque stepping forward at full strength behind a stencilled WE BUY line.
looks.groundSpec: The engine's tile lattice (COLS 4, ROWS 3, gap 28) but filled with assets/logos PNGs instead of cutouts — retheme_lab.mjs line 469 already preloads every logo into CUTOUT_ELS, so this is a pool swap, not new machinery. Ground is the palette's own c1: ck09 #f3f8fa (L 0.931), ca10 #d1effe (L 0.824), ck03 #f2f8f9. Marks are re-inked to the palette ink (ck09 #1f3c4c, ca10 #1d3c4b) at 18% for the field and 100% for the named make. NO DROP SHADOW ON A LATTICE CELL — a wordmark is flat artwork, not an object; the engine's shadow (rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur 26 offset 10/16) is for vehicles only. Scrim is capped at 0.16 of the ink, NOT the engine's default 0.6-0.72 dark wash, which would drown 18% type; legibility comes from a solid ink plate under the headline instead (the __tileBg branch already forces panels solid). Normalise by optical mass, never by box: wide wordmarks (ram-trucks 960x91, hyundai 960x124, toyota 960x159, dodge 960x168, kawasaki 960x172) take 0.86 of cell width; square emblems (bmw 960x960, honda 960x930, nissan 960x804, harley-davidson 960x745) take 0.46; tesla (960x1242, taller than wide) takes 0.40 of cell height. looks.collectionNote: FORECOURT is the shop's own lot, drawn in lot paint. Ten cards that all obey the same four rules, which is what makes them one family and not ten ideas: (1) IMAGERY IS VEHICLES, MARQUES OR PAPERWORK AND NOTHING ELSE — the only cutouts any card in this collection may use are the thirteen vehicle assets I verified by eye (car-sedan-front, car-sedan-rear, car-suv-side, car-front, car-truck-front, car-van-cargo, car-motorcycle-side, car-classic-side, car-damaged-front, car-keys, car-hand-keys-over, car-title-docs, car-wheel-tyre) plus the sixteen approved marque PNGs; no cash, no hands, no clipboards, no shields, no pins, no storefronts, no Apple scenes. (2) TYPE IS THE LOT'S OWN VOICE — a condensed or stencil display (stencil 60%, condensed 49%, the two best face styles in the data and the top of FIT.cars), a grotesque support, a mono or condensed numeral. No script, no handwriting, no blackletter anywhere in the collection. (3) COLOUR IS LOT PAINT — every palette sits in the blue/teal/indigo band with a warm accent: pale board (ck09 ck03 ck06 ca09 ca10 pp02), painted metal (du07 du08 cd06 du06), night (nn01 jw09 jw05 jw01), ruled paper (lp01 lp03 lp05 lp08 lp09). Nothing pink, orchid, violet or rose — which also keeps every card clear of the engine's own PALFIT.cars/trucks/vans/bikes avoid regexes. (4) ONE SHARED MARK — the LOT LINE: a pair of painted stall lines at 18-22 degrees running off one edge in ink or accent, becoming a hazard band on the van card, a coachline on the classic card and a ruled margin on the two paper cards. THE LAW THIS COLLECTION EXISTS TO ENFORCE: a make may be named only where the card can show that make. Only six makes have honest imagery on disk — HARLEYS (bikes-harley-davidson-motorcycle-1/2/3, bikes-cruiser-motorcycle-parked-1), FORDS and F-150S (trucks-ford-f-150-1/-3; -2 is titled F-250 so it is FORDS-only), CHEVYS and SILVERADOS (trucks-chevrolet-silverado-pickup-1/-3, both 1970s-80s square-bodies), TRANSITS (vans-ford-transit-van-1/2/3, all Courier/Connect), BMWS (cars-bmw-key-1/2/3 and cars-car-key-fob-1, keys not cars), and MERCEDES (car-front is the one cutout with a legible three-pointed-star grille badge). Every other make — TOYOTAS, HONDAS, NISSANS, JEEPS, TESLAS, HYUNDAIS, KIAS, DODGES, RAMS, TACOMAS, TUNDRAS, YAMAHAS, KAWASAKIS — has NO photograph and NO matching cutout, so it may be named only on the Marque Wall, where the wordmark itself is the image. That single rule is why this collection can carry the 32% category. Distinguishing it at a glance from the other nine: everything is a vehicle, a badge or a title document, standing on painted asphalt in blue lot paint under stencilled caps — no jewellery, no slabs, no devices, no cash fans, and never the graded-slab frame (that is Pokemon and sports only) or an assets/scenes Apple press image (the engine's own subjectFaults flags those as "apple scene on a cars card"). Every card carries (562) 999-4994, iphones.LA, and LONG BEACH / LAKEWOOD / DOWNEY / CARSON / TORRANCE; every star row is five; every claim is bounded to the engine's own sanctioned strings.

looks.groundSpec: The engine's own device wall, unchanged in structure: 4x3, gap 28, each cell one object, no overlap, shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.28) blur 26 offset 10/16. looks.name: Night Lot
looks.oneLine: One car standing on a dark blue lot under a single sodium lamp, stall lines running to a vanishing point off the right edge, with the pickup promise glowing in the accent.
looks.groundSpec: A drawn deep ground, built through drawGround the same way cast and tile are, never a photograph. Fill c1 (nn01 #0e253c at L 0.017, jw09 #054666 at L 0.054, jw05 #044a51 at L 0.055). One radial lamp glow of the accent (nn01 #fcaca5, jw09 #fdc0b7, jw05 #febbd3) at 12% centred on (0.72W, 0.18H) with radius 0.55W — warm light on cold paint, which is what a lot looks like at eight in the evening. Two painted stall lines in the pale ink (nn01 #d4dfeb, jw09 #d2e0ea) at 16%, converging toward a vanishing point off the right edge at 20 degrees. Grain at 3%. No window shadow — that belongs to the cast themes. The vehicle is a placed layer, not cast into the ground, at 620-720px wide with a 26px contact shadow directly under the tyres so it stands on the paint rather than floating. Money plate takes the accent with onAccent text. This theme is deep-only: on a pale palette the lamp glow has nothing to sit in and the card becomes a grey wash, so it does not run.

One car under one lamp — a second vehicle turns a lot at night into a dealership at night, which is somebody else's business.

looks.name: Chrome Cruiser
looks.oneLine: A real Harley photographed against a plain wall, the bar-and-shield in its own orange and black in the corner, deep indigo type stacked clear of the front wheel.
looks.groundSpec: The collection's only photograph, and it earns the exception because the photograph is of the make the headline names. Ground is bikes-harley-davidson-motorcycle-3 (a white Road King, front three-quarter, against a plain grey wall, 4800x3600) with the scrim taken from the engine's busy-photo branch: scrimColor c1 at 0.44 on jw01 #1f3e7a, 0.50 on nn01 #0e253c. On the black Softail (bikes-harley-davidson-motorcycle-1, brick pavers and grass behind it) push the scrim to 0.52 because the background is a garden and reads as somebody's house. Type stack takes the upper-left; the front wheel keeps the lower-right third. THE MARK IS PLACED IN ITS OWN COLOURS AND IS NEVER RE-INKED: harley-davidson.png is a full-colour shield — I probed it and the interior is opaque, orange #ff6600 on the shield with opaque white lettering inside an opaque black bar — so the engine's inkedLogo source-in fill would flatten it to a single-colour blob and erase the word HARLEY-DAVIDSON. Every other approved marque re-inks safely: toyota, ford, nissan, dodge, kawasaki are black silhouettes; honda #da251d, tesla #e82127, kia #c41230, yamaha-motor #f30711 are single-colour with transparent counters; chevrolet, jeep, ram-trucks, mercedes-benz and hyundai are open outline marks. The engine's forced bike element colours (#ff6a00, #ffb300, #e53935) happen to be Harley's own band and sit correctly on a deep indigo ground — which is also why this theme must stay in the indigo/blue band that PALFIT.bikes allows.
looks.imagery: A genuine Harley-Davidson and its own mark, together. looks.oneLine: A cream concours card: the pre-war coupe bled off the right edge, one accent coachline through the money word, and nothing else on the page.
looks.groundSpec: Pale cast branch on near-white grounds — ck06 #fbf5f3 at L 0.923, pp02 #fdf4ee at L 0.918, ck09 #f3f8fa at L 0.931 — but pulled back from the engine's defaults because a concours card wants air: ink at 12% rather than 20%, the accent-to-ink gradient at half strength, the diagonal window shadow at 0.42 rather than 0.58, and the scrim at 0.22 rather than 0.30. car-classic-side draws at k = min(670/2048, 993/1870) = 0.327 for 670x612. The collection's lot line becomes a coachline here: a single 3px rule in the accent (ck06 #9c3a05, pp02 #ac5d05, ck09 #0c658d) running the full card width along the money line's baseline. No vintage costume face and no distressed texture — the period comes from the car and the coachline, not from a font in fancy dress.
looks.imagery: car-classic-side: a black-and-cream 1930s coupe in side profile with whitewall tyres, cut at the front and rear by the file itself. That crop is the whole placement rule — it must bleed off the right edge so the cut reads as framing, never float mid-card where it reads as chopped. looks.oneLine: The wrecked sedan cast into blue paint with the crushed corner turned inward and the cash figure stencilled opposite it — the card that says a bad car is still worth money.
looks.groundSpec: Non-pale cast branch on du07 (#1ba3c7, L 0.306) and du08 (#5593ef, L 0.290): fill c1, white sheen 0.10, car-damaged-front drawn at k = min(670/1661, 993/1017) = 0.403 for 670x410 at (713, 562), rotated -0.12 rad, shadow blur 40 offset 24/30, then the window shadow at 0.50 and a scrim of c1 at 0.22. Lot line: a hazard chevron pair at the bottom-left in the accent (du07 #254b69, du08 #3c3e65) at 40%. On ca09 the pale branch runs — ink 20%, gradient, window shadow 0.58, scrim 0.30 — and the chevrons drop to 28% so a light card does not shout.

looks.name: Quote Slip
looks.oneLine: A ruled slip with the competitor named in slab caps, our line written under it in pen, and two keys lying on the paper — the card for someone who already has a number in their phone.
looks.groundSpec: Lined Paper family ground again, but a different sheet and a different geometry from Title Desk so the two do not twin: paper:grid or paper:dots rather than ruled, the slip drawn as a 62% x 44% panel in c1 with a 2px accent border and a torn bottom edge, tilted 2 degrees. c1 lp05 #e9f7f7 (L 0.906), lp09 #eaf7f2 (L 0.904); pen accent lp05 #06585c, lp09 #0c5b46. Highlighter and sticky again restricted to the blue or yellow end of the engine's fixed lists — #cfe8ff or #fff59d, and #d6ebff or #fff3a0 — never pink, violet or green. The collection's lot line becomes the slip's ruled underline beneath the competitor's name. On ck03 (Chalk, #f2f8f9, not a familyGround) the sheet is replaced by a flat near-white card with the same slip panel and a 3px accent rule; deep palettes do not run.
looks.imagery: car-keys at 240-300px lying across the corner of the slip — two unbranded black flip keys, the only key asset in the library with no maker's badge on it. Nothing else: the image is the piece of paper and the keys that come with the car.
mustShow: car-keys or car-hand-keys-over at 340px or less
a competitor named in the headline from CARVANA, CARMAX, KBB, AUTONATION or THE DEALER
neverShow: any competitor wordmark — naming them in type is comparative advertising, showing their mark implies endorsement
a specific competitor figure or a fabricated quote number
an apostrophe-S after a competitor name — WE MATCH CARVANA, never CARVANA'S
car-keys-fob — its leather fob carries another maker's badge, which under a competitor headline reads as a third brand on the card
eBay or Facebook Marketplace as the named target — a marketplace is a venue, not a buyer
looks.copy: Second-opinion voice: we assume they already have an offer and we talk about that offer, not about ourselves. Headline: WE MATCH CARMAX. Money line: THE SAME NUMBER, WITHOUT THE HOOPS. Selling point: We match the CarMax number without the hoops — no fees, no waiting, cash today. Second selling point: Screenshot your quote. We beat it or we say so. CTA: GET AN INSTANT OFFER. Five stars on the review row, always.
